senses.title: A quality of judgment without bias
senses.titleCN: 不因好恶而偏移的判断品质
senses.definition: the quality of judging a matter without letting preference for one side affect the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 裁断事情时不让对某一方的偏好影响结果的那种品质
senses.example: The panel's ruling was praised for its impartiality.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会的裁决因公正而受到称赞。
senses.why: The noun is built on an adjective that denies 'partial', so the word literally names the absence of taking a part; the positive virtue is defined by what it removes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在否定「偏向某一部分」的形容词之上，字面上命名的正是「不去取一部分」；这一正面德性由它所移除的东西来定义。

senses.title: Institutional neutrality of a court
senses.titleCN: 法院或仲裁机构的机构性中立
senses.definition: the position of a court or tribunal that stands apart from the parties and decides only on the record
senses.definitionCN: 法院或仲裁庭与当事人保持距离、只依卷宗裁断的立场
senses.example: The tribunal guarded its impartiality by barring private meetings with litigants.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁庭禁止与诉讼当事人私下会面，以守护自身的中立。
senses.why: Once the quality belongs to an institution rather than a person, it becomes a rule of conduct: the bench must be visibly separate from both sides.
senses.whyCN: 当这种品质属于机构而不是个人，它就变成行为规则：审判席必须在双方之外，而且让人看得见。

senses.title: Hearing both sides as procedure
senses.titleCN: 作为程序要求的兼听双方
senses.definition: the procedural duty to let each party present its case before a decision is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在作出决定之前让每一方陈述自己主张的程序义务
senses.example: Impartiality requires that both parties be heard, even when one case looks stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 公正要求双方都得到陈诉机会，即使一方理由看似更强。
senses.why: A fair mind needs a fair procedure to show itself, so the abstract quality turns into a step-by-step obligation.
senses.whyCN: 公正的心智需要公正的程序才能显现，于是这一抽象品质转化为一步步的义务。

senses.title: Weighing evidence equally
senses.titleCN: 以同一标准权衡双方证据
senses.definition: the practice of applying the same standards of proof and the same attention to evidence from either side
senses.definitionCN: 对两方提供的证据使用同一套证明标准、给予同等关注的做法
senses.example: Judges apply impartiality when they test both sets of records by the same standard.
senses.exampleCN: 法官用同一标准检验两套卷宗时，正是在践行公正。
senses.why: The scales image survives here most literally: equal weights, one beam.
senses.whyCN: 天平的形象在这里保留得最直接：同等的重量，同一根横梁。

senses.title: Objectivity in research and reporting
senses.definition: the quality of presenting findings or facts without letting the author's sympathies shape them
senses.definitionCN: 呈现研究结果或事实时不让作者的好恶塑造它们的品质
senses.example: The journal demands impartiality in the reporting of experimental results.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊要求实验结果的报道保持客观。
senses.why: The word left the courtroom and entered scholarship, where bias is measured against data rather than against litigants.
senses.whyCN: 这个词走出法庭进入学术，在那里偏见是以数据而不是以当事人为参照来衡量的。

senses.title: Political neutrality in public service
senses.titleCN: 公共服务中的政治中立
senses.definition: the duty of officials and broadcasters to serve all sides without favouring a party
senses.definitionCN: 官员与广播机构不偏向任何政党、为各方服务的义务
senses.example: The charter imposes impartiality on the public broadcaster.
senses.exampleCN: 章程把中立义务加在公共广播机构身上。
senses.why: In a democracy the same virtue is asked of institutions that hold power over everyone, so neutrality becomes a constitutional expectation.
senses.whyCN: 在民主制度中，同样的德性被要求于那些对所有人行使权力的机构，中立因此成为宪法层面的期待。

senses.title: The appearance of fairness
senses.definition: the condition of seeming unbiased, so that no reasonable observer could suspect favour
senses.definitionCN: 看起来没有偏向，使任何通情达理的旁观者都不会怀疑偏袒的状态
senses.example: A judge must retire from a case to preserve the appearance of impartiality.
senses.exampleCN: 法官必须退出某一案件，以维护公正的外表。
senses.why: Because trust is built on what can be seen, the word comes to cover not only the inner state but the visible absence of contact or interest.
senses.whyCN: 信任建立在可见之物上，因此这个词不只覆盖内心状态，也覆盖看得见的、没有往来与利害关系的状态。

senses.title: Detachment that can look cold
senses.definition: an aloof distance from others' concerns, criticised as indifference rather than praised as fairness
senses.definitionCN: 与他人所关切之事保持疏远距离，被批评为冷漠而不是被称赞为公正
senses.example: His impartiality at the family meeting felt like coldness to those who wanted comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 他在家庭会议上的不偏不倚，在那些想得到安慰的人看来像是冷淡。
senses.why: Any virtue has a shadow: the same refusal to take a side can be read as a refusal to care.
senses.whyCN: 任何德性都有阴影：同一种不站队的姿态，也可能被读作不愿关心。

intro.en: Impartiality is the noun of impartial, formed with the Latin negative prefix and partialis 'relating to a part'. It is a relatively late English formation, built to name the virtue of a judge rather than inherited whole from Latin.
intro.cn: impartiality 是 impartial 的名词形式，由拉丁语否定前缀与 partialis「与部分有关的」构成。它是英语较晚的造词，为命名裁判者的德性而造，并非整词从拉丁语继承。

items.en: Pars, partis meant 'part, share, side', and it supplied the idea that a person can take one side of a matter.
items.cn: pars（属格 partis）意为「部分、份额、一方」，它提供了「人可以取某一边」这一观念。

items.en: Partialis 'relating to a part' described what belongs to one side only; from it came the later sense of a person who favours one side.
items.cn: partialis 意为「与部分有关的」，描述只属于某一边的东西；由它后来发展出「偏向一方的人」这一意思。

items.en: The negative prefix denied the adjective, producing impartialis in later Latin and impartial in English.
items.cn: 否定前缀否定了这个形容词，在晚期拉丁语中构成 impartialis，进入英语后成为 impartial。

items.en: English writers of the seventeenth century added the quality noun ending to the adjective, at first in religious and legal disputes. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 十七世纪的英语作者给这个形容词加上表性质的名词词尾，最初用于宗教与法律争论。年代为约数。

items.en: In modern law and broadcasting the noun names a duty of institutions as much as a trait of persons; the extension belongs to the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 在现代法律与广播中，这个名词既指人的品格，也指机构的义务；这一扩展属于十九与二十世纪。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin word for a part but has taken different meanings; the second group offers near alternatives for the idea of not taking sides.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁语「部分」词，但意义已经分岔；第二组是「不站队」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: Not favouring one side; it describes a person or a decision, while the noun names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏向一方；它描述人或决定，而这个名词命名的是这种品质本身。

entries.definition: Relating to a part, and hence favouring one side; the negative prefix turns this adjective into the virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 与部分有关，因而偏向一方；否定前缀正是把这个形容词翻转成德性。

entries.definition: Bias toward one side, formed from partial with the same noun ending; it is the exact opposite of the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 偏向一边，由表示「部分的」的形容词加同一个名词词尾构成；它是本词的确切反义。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; it shares the Latin word for a part but refers to a physical fragment, not a side taken in judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；它共享拉丁语中「部分」一词，但指物理碎片，而不是判断中所站的立场。

entries.definition: The state of not supporting either side in a dispute; it often refers to states or mediators, while the entry word more often describes judges and procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 在争端中不支持任何一方的状态；它常指国家或调解人，而本词更多描述法官与程序。

entries.definition: The quality of being based on facts rather than feelings; it belongs to research and reporting, domains where impartiality is also used but with a focus on procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 以事实而非情感为依据的品质；它属于研究与报道，这些领域也用「公正」一词，但更侧重程序。

entries.definition: Even-handed treatment, often with a warmer tone and a link to rules and outcomes; impartiality stresses the absence of prior attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 平等待遇，语气往往更暖，并与规则和结果相连；本词更强调事先没有牵系。

entries.definition: A standing apart from people or interests; it can be a virtue of judgment but may also suggest emotional coldness.
entries.definitionCN: 与人或利害保持距离；它可以是判断的德性，也可能暗示情感上的冷淡。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin word for a part, the negative prefix, real derived words and real institutional phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「部分」的词、否定前缀、真实派生词与真实的机构用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a refusal: no part is taken, so no side is favoured.
normal.cn: 核心是一个拒绝：不取任何一部分，因此不偏向任何一方。

normal.en: The family runs impartial, impartially, impartiality and the opposite partiality.
normal.cn: 同族词包括形容词、副词、本词，以及反义的「偏向」。

normal.en: Courts speak of the impartiality of a judge and of the appearance of impartiality.
normal.cn: 法院会说「法官的公正」与「公正的外表」。

normal.en: Broadcasters are bound by political impartiality, a duty rather than a mood.
normal.cn: 广播机构受政治中立约束，那是一项义务而不是心情。

normal.en: The scales are the old picture: equal weights on one beam.
normal.cn: 天平是那幅旧图景：一根横梁上挂着同等的重量。

abstract.en: Picture a referee standing outside the touchline, never wearing either team's shirt.
abstract.cn: 想象一名裁判站在边线之外，从不穿任何一队的球衣。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that stays level because it carries the same two weights, not because it carries none.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁保持水平，是因为两端重量相同，而不是因为两端空无一物。

abstract.en: Picture a bright lamp that lights the whole room and warms no one in particular.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏明亮的灯照亮整个房间，却不会特别温暖某一个人。

examples.en: The review board is chosen for its impartiality rather than for its sympathy.
examples.cn: 评审委员会的选定看的是公正，而不是同情心。

examples.en: Any private contact between a judge and a party threatens the appearance of impartiality.
examples.cn: 法官与当事人之间的任何私下往来都会危及公正的外表。

examples.en: Statistical impartiality means the same test is applied to every sample.
examples.cn: 统计上的公正意味着对每个样本都使用同一套检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴偏私」——暗地里偏私就是不公正；把「偏私」整个否掉，剩下的就是不偏不倚。

root: 拉丁语 pars「部分」→ partialis「与部分有关的」→ 加否定前缀构成 impartial「不偏向任何一方的」→ 再加表性质的名词后缀构成 impartiality。词根链清楚；「部分」一词的更深来源不确定，与希腊语同族形式的对应属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from one act: refusing to take a part. Inside a court that act becomes an institution standing apart and a procedure of hearing both sides; applied to evidence it becomes equal weight; carried into research and public service it becomes objectivity and neutrality; pushed outward it becomes the appearance of fairness, and pushed too far, a cold detachment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一个动作长出：拒绝取一部分。在法庭里，这个动作成为与双方分开的机构，以及听取双方的程序；用在证据上，它是同等的重量；带到研究与公共服务中，它是客观与中立；向外推，它是公正的外表，推得过远，则是冷漠的超然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beam held level because neither pan has been secretly pressed down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根横梁保持水平，因为两只托盘都没有被暗中按下去。

branches.en: THE NEGATED PART: the core quality, defined by refusing to side with any part.
branches.cn: 被否定的部分：核心品质，由拒绝站到任何一部分来定义。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: an institution standing apart from the parties, and the duty to let both be heard.
branches.cn: 程序：与当事人分开的机构，以及让双方都被听取的义务。

branches.en: EQUAL WEIGHT: the scales read literally, the same standard applied to both sets of evidence.
branches.cn: 同等重量：天平的直读，对两方证据使用同一套标准。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE COURT: objectivity in research, and political neutrality in public service.
branches.cn: 法庭之外：研究中的客观，以及公共服务中的政治中立。

branches.en: SEEN AND FELT: the appearance of fairness, and the cold shadow that the same distance can cast.
branches.cn: 可见与感受：公正的外表，以及同一种距离可能投下的冷漠阴影。

intro.en: The word is built entirely from Latin pieces: a root for 'part', an adjective ending, a negative prefix and a noun ending. No Germanic element enters this family.
intro.cn: 这个词完全由拉丁语部件搭成：一个表示「部分」的词根、一个形容词词尾、一个否定前缀和一个名词词尾。这个家族里没有日耳曼语成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the root, the adjective and the negated adjective that produced the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了构成这个英语词的词根、形容词以及被否定的形容词。

items.meaning: the quality of not taking a side
items.meaningCN: 不站到任何一边的品质
items.example: The ruling was noted for its impartiality.
items.exampleCN: 这项裁决以公正著称。

items.example: An impartial panel reviewed the case.
items.exampleCN: 一个不偏不倚的小组复审了此案。

items.meaning: in a way that favours no side
items.meaningCN: 以不偏向任何一方的方式
items.example: The evidence was impartially weighed.
items.exampleCN: 证据被不偏不倚地权衡。

items.meaning: relating to a part; favouring one side
items.example: A partial reading of the record misled the court.
items.exampleCN: 对卷宗片面的解读误导了法庭。

items.example: The referee was accused of partiality.
items.exampleCN: 裁判被指偏向一方。

items.example: Each partner took an equal part of the profit.
items.exampleCN: 每位合伙人取得相等的利润份额。

items.example: The delay was partly caused by weather.
items.exampleCN: 延误差一部分由天气造成。

items.example: Dust particles filled the beam of light.
items.exampleCN: 灰尘颗粒填满了那道光柱。

items.example: The workers questioned the fairness of the division.
items.exampleCN: 工人们质疑这种分配是否公平。

latinEntries.structure: negated form of the adjective, late Latin

derivatives.zh: 不偏向任何一方的（否定前缀与表示「部分的」形容词结合，指裁决不站到某一部分的立场）
不偏不倚地（形容词加副词后缀，指以不偏向任何一方的方式）
偏向；偏心（表示「部分的」形容词加表性质的名词后缀，指偏向一方的倾向，与本词构成反义）
部分的；偏袒的（表示「部分」的词根加形容词后缀，指只涉及一部分，因而站到一方）

definition_zh: 宪法权利；宪法保障的基本权利；宪法上的权利
definition_en: a right guaranteed to people by a country's constitution and placed beyond ordinary legislative change
core_image: 一本摊开的宪法摆在法院台阶上，书页中一条被红线框住的条款，正挡住一扇正在关上的门
scene: 法院在判决中确认，集会自由属于宪法权利，政府不得以行政命令取消。The court held that freedom of assembly is a constitutional right which no administrative order may cancel.
sceneCN: 这里指「宪法明文保障、可用来对抗政府的基本权利」，对应第 1 个义项：由宪法确认、政府不能随意取消的权利；句意为法院认定集会自由属于此类权利。画面要点：摊开的宪法、被红线框住的条款、被挡住的门。

pos.zh: 宪法权利（可数，常用复数形式，指一组由宪法保障的权利）

derivatives.zh: 宪法的；符合宪法的（由「宪法」这一名词加形容词后缀构成，指与根本组织相关或经其许可）
依宪法地；从宪法角度看（形容词加副词后缀，指以宪法为尺度）
违宪的（否定前缀加形容词，指与宪法条文相抵触）
宪法；根本组织（由拉丁语「设立、安排」的动词加名词词尾构成，指一国根本结构的成文安排）

senses.title: A right written into the charter
senses.definition: an entitlement that the constitution itself names or clearly implies, so that it does not depend on an ordinary statute
senses.definitionCN: 宪法本身列明或明显蕴含的应享之权，因此不依赖普通法律而存在
senses.example: The court held that freedom of assembly is a constitutional right which no administrative order may cancel.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定集会自由属于宪法权利，任何行政命令都不能取消。
senses.why: The phrase joins a word for the state's founding arrangement to a word for a just claim, so the right is anchored in the document that creates the state.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示国家根本安排的名词与表示正当主张的名词连在一起，权利因此被锚定在创制国家的那份文件上。

senses.title: A shield against government action
senses.definition: a right that can be asserted against the state, limiting what officials may do to a person
senses.definitionCN: 可以针对国家主张的权利，用以限制官员能对个人做什么
senses.example: A constitutional right limits the search of a private home without a warrant.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法权利限制没有搜查令时对私人住宅的搜查。
senses.why: Most such rights are phrased as prohibitions on government, so the right works less as a grant than as a fence around power.
senses.whyCN: 这类权利多以对政府的禁令形式表述，因此它更像围住权力的一道栅栏，而不是一项授予。

senses.title: A rank above ordinary law
senses.titleCN: 位阶高于普通法律的权利
senses.definition: a right that ordinary legislation cannot remove or dilute, because it stands at a higher level in the legal order
senses.definitionCN: 普通立法不能取消或稀释的权利，因为它在法律秩序中处于更高位阶
senses.example: Because it is a constitutional right, the guarantee survives changes in the statute book.
senses.exampleCN: 由于它是宪法权利，这项保障不会因普通法令的变动而消失。
senses.why: The word for a founding arrangement implies a hierarchy: what is set at the base cannot be moved by what is built on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 表示根本安排的那个词本身就含有一个层级：设在基底的东西，不能被建在其上的东西挪动。

senses.title: A right that resists restriction
senses.titleCN: 难以被限制、需经严格审查的权利
senses.definition: a right that a court will let the state restrict only for a compelling reason and by the narrowest means
senses.definitionCN: 只有在理由极为充分、且手段最小时，法院才允许国家加以限制的权利
senses.example: Restrictions on a constitutional right must pass strict scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 对宪法权利的限制必须通过严格审查。
senses.why: Rank alone does not protect a right; the higher rank is enforced through a stricter test that the government must satisfy.
senses.whyCN: 位阶本身并不保护权利；较高的位阶是通过一套更严格的检验来落实的，而举证责任在政府一方。

senses.title: Procedural guarantees
senses.definition: rights concerned with how decisions are made, such as notice, a hearing and a reasoned decision
senses.definitionCN: 关乎决定如何作出的权利，例如获得通知、获得听审与获得说明理由的决定
senses.example: Due process is the constitutional right that the hearing must actually take place.
senses.exampleCN: 正当程序这项宪法权利意味着听审必须真正举行。
senses.why: A person cannot enjoy substantive rights without a procedure to claim them, so the charter protects the road as well as the destination.
senses.whyCN: 没有主张的程序，人就无法享有实体权利，因此宪法既保护目的地，也保护道路。

senses.title: Substantive freedoms
senses.definition: rights protecting what a person may say, believe, own or do, rather than how a decision is reached
senses.definitionCN: 保护个人可以说什么、信什么、拥有什么、做什么的权利，而不是关于决定如何作出的权利
senses.example: Speech and worship are substantive constitutional rights in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多国家，言论与礼拜都是实体性的宪法权利。
senses.why: The same document that sets out procedure also marks out areas the state may not enter at all, and those areas are the substantive core.
senses.whyCN: 同一份文件既规定了程序，也划出了国家完全不得进入的区域，那些区域就是实体核心。

senses.title: A right a court can enforce
senses.titleCN: 法院可以强制执行的权利
senses.definition: a right that a person may bring before a court and obtain a remedy for its breach
senses.definitionCN: 个人可以提交法院、并在其被侵害时获得救济的权利
senses.example: Without a remedy, a constitutional right would be only a promise on paper.
senses.exampleCN: 没有救济，宪法权利就只是纸上的承诺。
senses.why: A claim that cannot be heard is not a right in practice, so the enforceable sense grows from the legal meaning of a right as something a court will act on.
senses.whyCN: 不能被审理的主张在实践中不是权利，因此「可强制执行」这一层从权利的法律含义中长出来：法院会为之采取行动。

senses.title: A guarantee that resists amendment
senses.titleCN: 难以通过修宪变动的保障
senses.definition: a right whose removal would require the special and difficult procedure of constitutional amendment
senses.definitionCN: 要取消它必须走修宪这一特殊而艰难的程序的权利
senses.example: Changing that constitutional right would require a two-thirds vote in both houses.
senses.exampleCN: 要改变那项宪法权利，需在两院各取得三分之二多数。
senses.why: When a guarantee is placed in the charter, the cost of removing it rises from a simple majority to an amendment, and that cost is itself part of the protection.
senses.whyCN: 当一项保障被放进宪法，取消它的成本就从简单多数上升到修宪，而这个成本本身就是保护的一部分。

intro.en: Constitutional joins the noun constitution to an adjective ending; constitution descends from Latin constituere 'to set up'. Right is a Germanic word, not a Latin borrowing, though it shares an ancient root with Latin rectus. The phrase itself is a modern legal compound.
intro.cn: constitutional 由名词 constitution 加形容词词尾构成；constitution 出自拉丁语 constituere「设立」。right 是日耳曼语词，并非拉丁语借词，但它与拉丁语 rectus 共享一个古老词根。整个短语属现代法律复合词。

items.en: Statuere 'to set up, establish' is the verb at the base of the family, carrying the image of placing something so that it stands.
items.cn: statuere 意为「竖立、设立」，是整个词族的基干动词，含有把某物安置得能立住的形象。

items.en: Constituere joined the prefix for 'together' with statuere and described arranging a body, an office or an institution.
items.cn: constituere 把表示「共同」的前缀与 statuere 结合，描述对一个团体、职位或机构的安排。

items.en: Constitutio named an arrangement or an ordinance, and in Roman law it could mean an enactment issued by the emperor.
items.cn: constitutio 指一种安排或法令，在罗马法中可指皇帝颁布的敕令。

items.en: In English the noun came to mean the fundamental arrangement of a state, and its adjective followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 在英语中，这个名词逐渐指一个国家的根本安排，其形容词形式在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Riht meant 'straight, just, right' and supplied the word for a just claim long before anyone attached it to a written charter.
items.cn: riht 意为「直的、正当的、对的」，在人们把它与成文宪章联系起来之前很久，就已用来指正当的主张。

items.en: The phrase took its present sense in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, as written charters and judicial review spread. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法与司法审查的普及，这个短语在十八与十九世纪取得现今含义。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin verb for setting up; the second group holds other kinds of right that are often confused with this one.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一个表示「设立」的拉丁动词构成的词；第二组是常与本词混淆的其他类型的权利。

entries.definition: The fundamental text or arrangement of a state; it is the source that the adjective describes, not the right itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一个国家的根本文本或根本安排；它是形容词所描述的来源，而不是权利本身。

entries.definition: Forming an essential part of something; it describes what makes a thing what it is, not what a charter guarantees.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物本质部分的；它描述使一物成为该物的要素，而不是宪章保障的内容。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, or a voter in a district; the same verb underlies it, but neither sense concerns a guaranteed entitlement.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的组成部分，或选区中的选民；同一个动词是其底子，但两种意思都不涉及受保障的权利。

entries.definition: A right treated as basic to a legal order; in many systems it is the same set of guarantees, but the label stresses importance rather than the source document.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为某一法律秩序之基础的权利；在许多法系中它指同一组保障，但这个说法强调重要性而非来源文件。

entries.definition: A right given by an ordinary law, which the legislature can also narrow or repeal; it stands lower than the constitutional kind.
entries.definitionCN: 由普通法律赋予的权利，立法机关也可加以缩小或废止；它的位阶低于宪法权利。

entries.definition: Any entitlement recognised by law, whatever its source; it covers constitutional, statutory and judge-made rights alike.
entries.definitionCN: 法律承认的任何应享之权，不问来源；它同时涵盖宪法、法律与判例产生的权利。

entries.definition: A right said to belong to people by nature, before any document; it is a moral argument that a charter may later record.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为人生而固有、先于任何文件的权利；它是一种道德主张，宪章后来可能把它记录下来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb for setting up, the Germanic word for a just claim, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「设立」的动词、日耳曼语中表示正当主张的词、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: A constitution sets things up; a constitutional right is one of the things it sets beyond ordinary law.
normal.cn: 宪法把事物设立起来；宪法权利就是它设立在普通法律之上的那些事物之一。

normal.en: The family runs constitution, constitutional, constitutionally and unconstitutional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括「宪法」、形容词、副词与否定形式。

normal.en: Rights in a charter act as fences around government power rather than gifts handed out.
normal.cn: 宪章中的权利更像围住政府权力的栅栏，而不是被分发的礼物。

normal.en: A statutory right can be repealed by a new statute; a constitutional one needs an amendment.
normal.cn: 法律权利可被新法律废止；宪法权利则需要修宪。

normal.en: The Germanic word for right is related to the Latin word for straight, which is why a right and a straight line feel connected.
normal.cn: 表示「权利」的日耳曼语词与拉丁语中表示「直」的词同源，所以权利与直线在感觉上相通。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab laid at the bottom of a building, so deep that later floors cannot move it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板铺在建筑的最底层，埋得那样深，以至于上面各层都无法挪动它。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawn on a map before any building is allowed inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象在任何人获准进入之前，地图上先画好的一道栅栏。

abstract.en: Picture a door that can be closed by many hands but opened only by a key kept in a locked drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，许多人都能关上，却只有一把存放在上锁抽屉里的钥匙才能打开。

examples.en: The right to a hearing is a constitutional right in that system.
examples.cn: 在该法系中，获得听审的权利是一项宪法权利。

examples.en: Officials argued that the order did not touch any constitutional right.
examples.cn: 官员辩称该命令并未触及任何宪法权利。

examples.en: A constitutional right cannot be abolished by a simple majority vote.
examples.cn: 宪法权利不能被简单多数票废除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「宪法里的那张票」——把权利写在国家根本章程上，就成了谁都拿不走的一张票。

root: constitution 出自拉丁语 constituere「设立、安排」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 statuere「竖立」构成，再经 constitutio「安排、敕令」进入英语；right 出自古英语 riht「直的、正当的」，属日耳曼语词，与拉丁语 rectus「直的」同源，源头可追至印欧语中表示「使直、统治」的词根，该词根形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings circle one anchor: a claim fixed in the founding document. From that anchor come the shield against the state, the rank above ordinary law, the strict test that guards the rank, the split between procedure and substance, the remedy that makes the claim real, and the high cost of amendment that keeps it in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个锚点：固定在建国文件中的一项主张。从这个锚点分出：对抗国家的盾牌、高于普通法律的位阶、守护位阶的严格检验、程序与实体的分工、使主张成真的救济，以及使它留在原处的修宪高成本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause printed in the founding charter, standing between a person and the machinery of the state.
core.cn: 核心意象：印在建国宪章里的一条条款，立在个人与国家机器之间。

branches.en: THE ANCHOR: the entitlement named in the charter itself.
branches.cn: 锚点：宪章本身列明的应享之权。

branches.en: SHIELD AND REMEDY: the claim against the state, and the court that can act on it.
branches.cn: 盾牌与救济：针对国家的主张，以及能据此行动的法院。

branches.en: RANK AND RIGIDITY: a level above ordinary law, and the amendment cost that keeps it there.
branches.cn: 位阶与刚性：高于普通法律的层级，以及把它留在那里的修宪成本。

branches.en: LIMIT AND PROCEDURE: the strict test for restriction, and the guarantees about how decisions are made.
branches.cn: 限制与程序：限制权利时的严格检验，以及关于决定如何作出的保障。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: the freedoms the state may not enter at all.
branches.cn: 实体：国家完全不得进入的那些自由领域。

intro.en: Two histories meet in this phrase: a Latin verb for establishing, which gives the whole constitution family, and a Germanic adjective for straightness and justice, which gives right and its derived words.
intro.cn: 两段历史在这个短语里相遇：一个表示「设立」的拉丁动词给出整个「宪法」词族，一个表示「直」与「正当」的日耳曼形容词给出「权利」及其派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below belong to the constitution side of the phrase. Right has a Latin cousin meaning 'straight', but the English word itself was not borrowed from that cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式属于短语中「宪法」这一边。「权利」有一个意为「直」的拉丁同源词，但英语中的这个词本身并非从该同源词借入。

items.meaning: a basic entitlement fixed in the founding charter
items.meaningCN: 固定在建国宪章中的基本应享之权
items.example: The court treated the claim as a constitutional right.
items.exampleCN: 法院把这项主张视为宪法权利。

items.meaning: of or consistent with the constitution
items.example: The reform required a constitutional amendment.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革需要一次宪法修正。

items.meaning: the fundamental arrangement of a state
items.example: The constitution divides power among three branches.
items.exampleCN: 宪法把权力分给三个分支。

items.meaning: the quality of being consistent with the charter
items.example: The court reviewed the constitutionality of the statute.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了该法令是否符合宪法。

items.example: The search was ruled unconstitutional.
items.exampleCN: 那次搜查被裁定违宪。

items.meaning: a just claim; straight and correct
items.meaningCN: 正当的主张；直的、正确的
items.example: Every citizen has the right to petition.
items.exampleCN: 每个公民都有请愿的权利。

items.meaning: in accordance with a just claim
items.example: The heir returned to his rightful place.
items.exampleCN: 继承人回到了他合法应有的位置。

items.example: She rightfully demanded a receipt.
items.exampleCN: 她正当地要求一张收据。

items.meaning: a legal priority to pass over land or road
items.example: Pedestrians have the right of way at this crossing.
items.exampleCN: 在这个路口行人有优先通行权。

latinEntries.meaning: to set up, cause to stand

derivatives.zh: 宪法的；符合宪法的（由「宪法」这一名词加形容词后缀构成，指与根本组织相关或经其许可）
依宪法地（形容词加副词后缀，指以宪法为尺度）
违宪的（否定前缀加形容词，指与宪法条文相抵触）
合法的；正当的（表示「正当」的名词加形容词后缀，指依正当主张而应得）

definition_zh: 民权；公民权（法律上平等、不受歧视的权利）
definition_en: the rights of citizens to equal treatment under the law and to take part in public life without discrimination
core_image: 一队不同肤色与出身的人并排站在同一道门槛前，门槛上的横木已被拆掉，所有人踩在同一级台阶
scene: 上世纪的游行队伍要求结束公共场所的种族隔离，把民权写进法律。Marchers demanded an end to segregation in public places and pressed for civil rights to be written into law.
sceneCN: 这里指「公民在法律上应受平等对待的一组权利」，对应第 1 个义项：不受歧视地享有平等待遇；句意为游行队伍要求结束公共场地的种族隔离，并把民权写入法律。画面要点：同一道门槛、被拆掉的横木、并排站立的人群。

pos.zh: 民权；公民权（通常作复数使用；作定语时用单数形式）

derivatives.zh: 公民的；民事的；有礼貌的（拉丁语中表示「公民」的名词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，指与公民和城邦有关）
礼貌；谦恭（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，语义由「公民的」转向「合乎公民交往礼仪的」）
平民；非军人（形容词加表人的名词后缀，指不属于军队的公民）
以民事方式；有礼貌地（形容词加副词后缀，指按公民间的方式行事）

senses.title: Equal standing before the law
senses.definition: the right of every citizen to be treated by the law on the same terms as everyone else
senses.definitionCN: 每个公民都有权在法律上受到与其他人相同的对待
senses.example: Marchers demanded an end to segregation in public places and pressed for civil rights to be written into law.
senses.exampleCN: 游行队伍要求结束公共场所的种族隔离，并推动把民权写入法律。
senses.why: The plural phrase begins from the oldest legal idea in the family: the citizen's standing in the city and its courts, extended to everyone equally.
senses.whyCN: 这个复数短语从该词族最古老的法律观念出发：公民在城邦及其法庭中的地位，并被推广到人人平等。

senses.title: Access to public places without discrimination
senses.titleCN: 不受歧视地进入公共场所
senses.definition: the right to use schools, transport, hotels and other public facilities on the same terms as other citizens
senses.definitionCN: 与其他公民同等使用学校、交通、旅馆及其他公共设施的权利
senses.example: The bus boycott tested whether civil rights covered public transport.
senses.exampleCN: 那场抵制公交的运动检验了民权是否涵盖公共交通。
senses.why: Equality before the law means little if the courthouse door is open but the station door is shut, so access became the first battlefield.
senses.whyCN: 如果法院的门开着而车站的门关着，法律面前的平等就所剩无几，因此进入场所的权利成为第一战场。

senses.title: The ballot
senses.definition: the right to vote and to stand for office without being excluded by race, sex or property qualifications
senses.definitionCN: 不因种族、性别或财产资格而被排除的投票权与参选权
senses.example: A central demand was that civil rights include the ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 一项核心要求是让民权包含选举权。
senses.why: A citizen who cannot vote cannot correct the laws that treat him unequally, so the vote is the mechanism that makes the other claims enforceable.
senses.whyCN: 不能投票的公民无法纠正那些不平等对待他的法律，因此选举权是使其他主张得以落实的机制。

senses.title: Speech, assembly and worship
senses.titleCN: 言论、集会与信仰的自由
senses.definition: the freedoms to speak, gather, organise and worship without state interference
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家干预地言论、集会、组织与礼拜的自由
senses.example: Civil rights in that charter include freedom of assembly and of worship.
senses.exampleCN: 那部宪章中的民权包括集会与信仰自由。
senses.why: To demand rights in public is itself an exercise of them, so the freedoms of speech and assembly are both the goal and the method of the struggle.
senses.whyCN: 在公共场合主张权利，本身就是行使这些权利，因此言论与集会的自由既是目标，也是斗争的方法。

senses.title: Due process and a remedy
senses.definition: the right to fair procedure, notice and a court that can hear a complaint of unequal treatment
senses.definitionCN: 获得公平程序、获得通知，以及由法院审理不平等待遇申诉的权利
senses.example: Civil rights are hollow unless a court will hear the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 如果法院不受理申诉，民权就是空的。
senses.why: The plural claims are enforceable only through procedure, so the family's legal core reappears as the right to be heard.
senses.whyCN: 这些复数的主张只有通过程序才能落实，因此这个词族的法律内核又以「获得听审」的形式重现。

senses.title: Equal chances in work and school
senses.titleCN: 就业与教育中的平等机会
senses.definition: the right not to be refused a job, a place or a promotion on discriminatory grounds
senses.definitionCN: 不因歧视性理由而被拒绝工作、入学名额或晋升的权利
senses.example: The ruling extended civil rights to hiring and admission.
senses.exampleCN: 该裁决把民权扩展到录用与招生。
senses.why: Once public access is secured, the same logic moves inward to the institutions that distribute opportunity, where exclusion is less visible but just as real.
senses.whyCN: 一旦公共场所的进入权得到保障，同样的逻辑就向内进入分配机会的机构，那里的排斥不那么显眼，却同样真实。

senses.title: The historical movement
senses.definition: the organised campaign, especially in the mid-twentieth-century United States, against racial segregation and exclusion
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指二十世纪中叶美国反对种族隔离与排斥的有组织运动
senses.example: The photographs of that civil rights campaign changed public opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 那场民权运动的照片改变了公众舆论。
senses.why: A set of legal claims became the name of the movement that fought for them, so the phrase now also names a period and a struggle.
senses.whyCN: 一组法律主张变成了为它们而战的那场运动的名字，因此这个短语现在也指一个时期与一场斗争。

senses.title: A field of law and study
senses.titleCN: 作为法律部门与研究领域
senses.definition: the branch of law, and the academic subject, concerned with protection against discrimination
senses.definitionCN: 以保护人们免受歧视为内容的那个法律部门与学术科目
senses.example: She teaches civil rights alongside constitutional law.
senses.exampleCN: 她与宪法学一起教授民权法。
senses.why: When the claims acquired statutes, agencies and casebooks, the plural phrase also became the label of a professional field.
senses.whyCN: 当这些主张有了法令、机构与判例教材，这个复数短语也就成了一个专业领域的名称。

intro.en: Civil comes from Latin civilis, an adjective from civis 'citizen'. Right is the Germanic word for a just claim. The plural phrase civil rights is a modern narrowing to equal treatment and public participation; earlier civil law meant the law of citizens.
intro.cn: civil 出自拉丁语 civilis，是名词 civis「公民」的形容词；right 是日耳曼语中表示正当主张的词。复数短语 civil rights 属现代用法，专指平等待遇与公共参与；早先的 civil law 指公民之法。

items.en: Civis 'citizen' named a member of the civitas, the body of people who share a city and its law, as distinct from a foreigner or a slave.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民」，指城邦这一共享城市与法律的群体中的成员，与外国人或奴隶相区别。

items.en: Civilis 'of a citizen, civic' described what belongs to citizens, including the law that governed them rather than soldiers or priests.
items.cn: civilis 意为「公民的、城邦的」，描述属于公民的事物，包括管束公民而非军人或祭司的那套法律。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective into English, at first in the phrase civil law, the law of citizens, which is still the name of a legal tradition.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于「公民之法」这一短语，该短语至今仍是某一大法系的名称。

items.en: Riht supplied the word for a just claim, and its plural named a set of such claims held by a person or a group.
items.cn: riht 提供了表示正当主张的词，其复数形式指个人或群体所持的一组此类主张。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the plural phrase narrowed to the claims of groups excluded from equal treatment, above all in the United States. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，这个复数短语收窄为被排斥于平等待遇之外的群体所提出的主张，尤以美国为典型。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for a citizen but has moved into politeness, the military and civic life; the second group distinguishes this phrase from neighbouring kinds of right.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语中「公民」一词，但已转向礼貌、军旅与城邦生活；第二组把本短语与相邻类型的权利区分开。

entries.definition: Of citizens, or of non-military and non-religious matters; it can also mean polite, a sense that grew far from the courtroom.
entries.definitionCN: 公民的，或非军事、非宗教事务的；它也可指有礼貌，这一意思已离法庭很远。

entries.definition: A person who is not in the armed forces; the ending marks a person, so the word never names a set of claims.
entries.definitionCN: 不在军队中的人；词尾标示的是人，因此这个词从不指一组主张。

entries.definition: Polite behaviour between people; it comes from the same adjective but describes manners, not entitlements.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间的礼貌行为；它出自同一个形容词，但描述礼节，而不是应享之权。

entries.definition: Relating to a city or to citizens' duties; it points to obligations and urban life rather than to protected claims.
entries.definitionCN: 与城市或公民义务有关的；它指向义务与城市生活，而不是受保护的主张。

entries.definition: Entitlements said to belong to every person simply by being human; they are wider in scope and rest on international law, while the entry phrase rests on citizenship.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为仅因作为人而属于每个人的应享之权；范围更宽，依据是国际法，而本短语的依据是公民身份。

entries.definition: Rights to vote, hold office and take part in government; they are one part of the entry phrase rather than its whole.
entries.definitionCN: 投票、担任公职与参与治理的权利；它们是本短语的一部分，而不是全部。

entries.definition: Any entitlements recognised by law, whatever their source; the entry phrase names a particular family of them.
entries.definitionCN: 法律承认的任何应享之权，不问来源；本短语只指其中一个特定的家族。

entries.definition: Freedoms from state restraint, such as speech and movement; they overlap with the entry phrase but stress absence of interference rather than equality.
entries.definitionCN: 免于国家约束的自由，例如言论与行动；它们与本短语重叠，但强调不受干预，而不是平等。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin citizen, the Germanic claim, real derived words and real historical phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中的「公民」、日耳曼语中的「主张」、真实派生词与真实历史用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is a citizen, so the phrase begins with membership in a community and its law.
normal.cn: 词根是「公民」，因此这个短语从一个人对共同体及其法律的归属开始。

normal.en: The family runs civil, civility, civilian, civilly and citizen.
normal.cn: 同族词包括形容词、礼貌、平民、副词形式与公民。

normal.en: The phrase fights on four fronts: the ballot, the bus, the school and the courtroom.
normal.cn: 这个短语在四条战线上作战：选票、公交车、学校与法庭。

normal.en: Civil law once meant the law of citizens; the plural phrase later narrowed to equal treatment.
normal.cn: 「公民之法」早先指公民的法律；后来这个复数短语收窄为平等待遇。

normal.en: The movement gave the phrase a date and a face, not just a definition.
normal.cn: 那场运动给了这个短语一个年代与一批面孔，而不只是定义。

abstract.en: Picture a queue where the rope has been removed, so no one is sorted into a separate line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍前的隔绳被撤掉，没有人再被分到另一条线里。

abstract.en: Picture four doors in a row, marked school, ballot, court and bus, all opening with the same key.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的四扇门，分别写着学校、选票、法庭与公交，全都用同一把钥匙打开。

abstract.en: Picture a march that is both the demand and the proof: people walking together are already using the freedom they ask for.
abstract.cn: 想象一场既是要求、也是证明的游行：同行的人已经在使用他们所要求的那种自由。

examples.en: The law was rewritten to protect civil rights in hiring.
examples.cn: 法律被修改，以保护录用环节中的民权。

examples.en: She studied civil rights as part of her constitutional law course.
examples.cn: 她在宪法学课程中研习民权法。

examples.en: A court that will not hear the complaint leaves civil rights on paper.
examples.cn: 法院若不受理申诉，民权就只留在纸上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「公民之权」——先有公民身份，才有同等走进同一道门的资格；把它拆成选票、校门、车门与法庭四件事来记。

root: civil 出自拉丁语 civilis，源自 civis「公民」，civis 的更深来源一般认为是印欧语中表示「躺卧、定居」的词根，该形式属重构形式；right 出自古英语 riht「直的、正当的」，属日耳曼语词，与拉丁语 rectus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings spread outward from citizenship. The core is equal standing; from it come access to public places, the ballot and the freedoms of speech and assembly; procedure makes those claims enforceable; equal opportunity carries them indoors; and the organised struggle plus its law books give the phrase a history and a profession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从公民身份向外铺开。核心是平等的地位；由此分出进入公共场所、选票以及言论与集会的自由；程序使这些主张可以落实；平等机会把它们带进室内；而有组织的斗争与它的法律教科书，则给了这个短语一段历史与一门职业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same step at the same threshold, with no separate entrance for anyone.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一道门槛前的同一级台阶，没有人需要另走一个入口。

branches.en: EQUAL STANDING: the legal core, one standard of treatment for every citizen.
branches.cn: 平等地位：法律内核，对每个公民使用同一套待遇标准。

branches.en: ACCESS: the bus, the school and the workplace, where exclusion is felt in daily life.
branches.cn: 进入：公交车、学校与工作场所，排斥在日常生活中被感受到的地方。

branches.en: VOICE: the ballot and the freedoms of speech and assembly, which let citizens act together.
branches.cn: 发声：选票以及言论与集会的自由，使公民能够共同行动。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND FIELD: the court that hears the claim, and the body of law that grew around it.
branches.cn: 程序与领域：审理主张的法院，以及围绕它生长出来的法律体系。

branches.en: STRUGGLE: the movement that turned a legal phrase into a period of history.
branches.cn: 斗争：把一组法律用语变成一段历史的运动。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin adjective for civic life to a Germanic noun for a just claim; the derived family splits along the same line, with civic words on one side and rightful ones on the other.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示城邦生活的拉丁形容词与一个表示正当主张的日耳曼名词连在一起；派生家族也沿同一条线分开，一边是城邦系词，一边是权利系词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below supply the citizen half of the phrase; the right half is Germanic and only its distant cousin appears in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式提供短语中「公民」的那一半；「权利」那一半属日耳曼语，拉丁语中只有它的远亲形式。

items.meaning: claims to equal treatment held by citizens
items.meaningCN: 公民所持的平等待遇主张
items.example: The statute protects civil rights in public housing.
items.exampleCN: 该法令保护公共住房中的民权。

items.example: The dispute was settled in a civil manner.
items.exampleCN: 这场争端以文明的方式解决。

items.example: The debate lost its civility after midnight.
items.exampleCN: 辩论在午夜之后失去了礼貌。

items.meaning: a person outside the armed forces
items.example: Aid was sent to the civilian population.
items.exampleCN: 援助被送往平民。

items.meaningCN: 有礼貌地；以文明的方式
items.example: The neighbours settled the matter civilly.
items.exampleCN: 邻居们文明地解决了此事。

items.meaning: a member of a state with its rights and duties
items.meaningCN: 享有权利并承担义务的国家成员
items.example: Every citizen may vote in the district.
items.exampleCN: 每位公民都可以在本区投票。

items.meaning: the status of being a citizen
items.example: She applied for citizenship after ten years.
items.exampleCN: 她十年后申请了公民身份。

items.meaning: relating to a city or to citizens' duties
items.meaningCN: 与城市或公民义务有关的
items.example: The mayor spoke about civic pride.
items.exampleCN: 市长谈到市民的自豪感。

items.example: The tenant has a right to a written notice.
items.exampleCN: 租户有权获得书面通知。

latinEntries.meaning: citizenship; the body of citizens; a city
latinEntries.meaningCN: 公民身份；公民群体；城邦

derivatives.zh: 公民的；民事的；有礼貌的（拉丁语中表示「公民」的名词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，指与公民和城邦有关）
礼貌；谦恭（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，语义由「公民的」转向「合乎公民交往礼仪的」）
平民；非军人（形容词加表人的名词后缀，指不属于军队的公民）
公民身份（表示「公民」的名词加表身份的名词后缀，指享有权利与义务的成员资格）

definition_zh: 人权；人作为人而享有的基本权利
definition_en: the basic entitlements that belong to every person simply by being human, without regard to nationality or status
core_image: 一张没有写名字的证件照嵌进一扇门，门后所有人不分国籍都能走进同一间屋
scene: 战后起草的宣言把免于恐惧与免于匮乏列为所有人的权利。The declaration drafted after the war set freedom from fear and freedom from want among the human rights of all people.
sceneCN: 这里指「仅因作为人而属于每个人的基本权利」，对应第 1 个义项：不依赖国籍、身份或地位而存在的应享之权；句意为战后宣言把免于恐惧与免于匮乏列入所有人的人权。画面要点：无名证件照、敞开的大门、所有人共处的一间屋。

pos.zh: 人权（通常作复数；作定语时用单数形式）

derivatives.zh: 人的；人类的（拉丁语中表示「人」的名词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，指属于人的）
人性；人类整体（形容词加表性质或集合的名词后缀，由个体属性转为整类存在）
人道主义的；人道救援的（形容词加表「主义、从事者」的后缀，指以减轻人的苦难为宗旨）
无人性的；残酷的（否定前缀加形容词，指缺少人应有的同情与节制）
无人性；残忍（否定前缀加表性质的名词，指残酷对待他人的状态）

senses.title: Entitlements that come with being human
senses.titleCN: 因作为人而固有的应享之权
senses.definition: rights said to belong to a person at birth, before any citizenship, contract or statute is considered
senses.definitionCN: 被认为人一出生就拥有的权利，先于任何公民身份、契约或法律而被考虑
senses.example: The declaration drafted after the war set freedom from fear and freedom from want among the human rights of all people.
senses.exampleCN: 战后起草的宣言把免于恐惧与免于匮乏列入所有人的人权。
senses.why: The phrase joins the noun for the human species to the noun for a just claim, so the claim is attached to the species rather than to a passport.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示人类的名词与表示正当主张的名词连在一起，于是主张被系在物种上，而不是系在一本护照上。

senses.title: Rights that cannot be given away
senses.titleCN: 不可让渡、不可剥夺的性质
senses.definition: the quality of such rights as incapable of being traded, waived or removed by any authority
senses.definitionCN: 此类权利不能被交易、放弃或被任何权力机关取消的性质
senses.example: Because they are inalienable, human rights cannot be signed away in a contract.
senses.exampleCN: 由于人权不可让渡，它们不能在合同中被签掉。
senses.why: If a right belongs to a person merely as a person, there is no moment at which it could be surrendered, and that logic produces the word inalienable.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项权利仅因人是人而属于他，就不存在可以交出它的时刻，这一逻辑产生了「不可让渡」这个说法。

senses.title: Protection under international law
senses.definition: the body of treaties, courts and monitoring bodies that turn the claims into obligations between states
senses.definitionCN: 把主张转化为国家间义务的条约、法院与监督机构的总和
senses.example: A regional court may hear a complaint under human rights law.
senses.exampleCN: 区域法院可依人权法审理申诉。
senses.why: A claim that reaches beyond every national border needs a forum beyond every national border, so the phrase acquires an international legal apparatus.
senses.whyCN: 超越一切国界的主张需要超越一切国界的论坛，因此这个短语获得了一套国际法律装置。

senses.title: Civil and political rights
senses.definition: the half of the field concerned with speech, voting, assembly and protection from arbitrary detention
senses.definitionCN: 该领域中关乎言论、投票、集会以及免于任意拘押的那一半
senses.example: Freedom of speech is the best-known of the civil and political human rights.
senses.exampleCN: 言论自由是公民与政治人权中最著名的一项。
senses.why: The first generation of the modern catalogue came from the struggle against arbitrary power, so it mirrors the older civil and political claims.
senses.whyCN: 现代权利清单的第一代来自对抗任意权力的斗争，因此它与更早的公民与政治主张相映照。

senses.title: Economic, social and cultural rights
senses.definition: the half of the field concerned with work, food, housing, health, education and shared culture
senses.definitionCN: 该领域中关乎工作、食物、住房、健康、教育与共享文化的那一半
senses.example: The right to education belongs to the economic and social side of human rights.
senses.exampleCN: 受教育权属于人权的经济与社会这一面。
senses.why: A person who is free to speak but has no food is not in fact free, so the catalogue widened from restraint to provision.
senses.whyCN: 一个可以自由发言却没有食物的人，事实上并不自由，因此这份清单从「不受约束」扩展到「得到供给」。

senses.title: A minimum in wartime
senses.definition: the irreducible protections that apply even in armed conflict, where ordinary law has broken down
senses.definitionCN: 即便在武装冲突、普通法律已失效时仍然适用的不可削减的保护
senses.example: Even in war, human rights set a floor below which no treatment may fall.
senses.exampleCN: 即便在战争中，人权也划出一条任何人不得越过的底线。
senses.why: The phrase proves its seriousness where law is weakest, so humanitarian law borrows it to mark the floor that survives a battlefield.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语在法律最薄弱之处证明自己的分量，因此人道法借用它来标出战场上也仍然存在的底线。

senses.title: A moral claim, not only a legal one
senses.titleCN: 作为道义主张，而不只是法律权利
senses.definition: the use of the phrase to criticise governments even where no court can enforce the claim
senses.definitionCN: 在没有任何法院能强制执行时，仍用这个短语来批评政府的用法
senses.example: Amnesty reports appeal to human rights even where treaties are not ratified.
senses.exampleCN: 大赦报告即使在没有批准条约的地方，也诉诸人权。
senses.why: Because the claim rests on being human rather than on being governed, it can be asserted against any state, enforceable or not.
senses.whyCN: 由于主张的依据是「作为人」而不是「受某国治理」，它可以对任何国家提出，无论能否强制执行。

senses.title: The argument over universality
senses.definition: the criticism that the catalogue reflects one culture's values and should not be imposed on all
senses.definitionCN: 认为这份清单反映某一种文化的价值、不应强加于所有人的批评
senses.example: The debate over human rights turns on whether the list is universal or local.
senses.exampleCN: 关于人权的争论，关键在于这份清单是普遍的还是地方性的。
senses.why: A word built on the whole species claims a scope wider than any culture, and exactly that width is what the criticism attacks.
senses.whyCN: 一个建立在整个人类之上的词，声称拥有比任何文化都更宽的范围，而批评攻击的正是这份宽度。

intro.en: Human descends from Latin humanus, an adjective from homo 'human being'. The deeper origin of homo is disputed, and a link with a word for earth remains a hypothesis. Right is Germanic. The plural phrase became global only in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: human 出自拉丁语 humanus，是名词 homo「人」的形容词；homo 的更深来源有争议，把它与表示「土地」的词相连仍属假说。right 属日耳曼语。这个复数短语直到二十世纪才成为全球性说法。

items.en: Homo meant 'human being, man' and stands behind the whole family. Its deeper origin is uncertain; one long-standing suggestion links it to a word for earth, but that link is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: homo 意为「人、人类」，是整个词族背后的名词。其更深来源不确定；一种流传较久的说法把它与表示「土地」的词相连，但那属假说，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Humanus 'of a person, humane' supplied the adjective, and it could already mean kind or gentle as well as merely belonging to people.
items.cn: humanus 意为「人的、有人情的」，提供了形容词，且早已既可指「属于人的」，也可指「仁慈温和的」。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective into English, where human first described what belongs to people and later, in a separate branch, what is kind.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带入英语；在英语中它先指「属于人的」，后来在另一支上指「仁慈的」。

items.en: Riht supplied the Germanic word for a just claim; its plural named a set of claims rather than a single entitlement.
items.cn: riht 提供了日耳曼语中表示正当主张的词；其复数形式指一组主张，而不是单独一项。

items.en: Writers of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries argued that certain claims follow from human nature itself, preparing the vocabulary that the modern phrase would use.
items.cn: 十七与十八世纪的作者主张某些权利主张源自人的本性本身，为现代短语将使用的词汇作了准备。

items.en: The universal declaration of 1948 fixed the phrase in global usage; the document's date is exact, while its wider adoption spread over the following decades.
items.cn: 1948 年的世界宣言把这个短语固定为全球用语；该文件的年代确切，而其更广泛的采纳则在此后数十年间铺开。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for a human being but has drifted into kindness, collective existence and relief work; the second group places the phrase among neighbouring kinds of claim.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语中表示「人」的词，但已漂向仁慈、整类存在与救援工作；第二组把本短语放进相邻类型的主张之中。

entries.definition: Kind and merciful, especially in treating people or animals; it comes from the same adjective but describes a temper, not a right.
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈而有同情心，尤指对待人或动物时；它出自同一个形容词，但描述性情，而不是权利。

entries.definition: All human beings collectively, or the quality of being humane; it names a group or a virtue, never a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 全体人类，或仁慈的品质；它命名一个群体或一种德性，从不指一项主张。

entries.definition: Concerned with reducing suffering, as in aid or law; it describes activity, while the entry phrase names entitlements.
entries.definitionCN: 以减轻苦难为宗旨，如援助或法律；它描述活动，而本短语命名的是应享之权。

entries.definition: Within the limits of human ability, as in humanly possible; it measures capacity rather than asserting a right.
entries.definitionCN: 在人的能力范围之内，如「人力所能及」；它衡量能力，而不是主张权利。

entries.definition: Claims to equal treatment held by citizens under a state's law; the entry phrase is wider and rests on being human rather than on membership.
entries.definitionCN: 公民依国家法律所持的平等待遇主张；本短语范围更宽，依据是「作为人」而不是成员资格。

entries.definition: Rights said to follow from human nature before any government; the entry phrase inherits the argument but adds an international legal apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为先于任何政府、源自人性的权利；本短语继承了这一论证，但增添了国际法律装置。

entries.definition: Freedoms from interference, such as speech and religion; they cover part of the entry phrase but say nothing about food, work or health.
entries.definitionCN: 免于干预的自由，例如言论与信仰；它们覆盖本短语的一部分，却不涉及食物、工作或健康。

entries.definition: Protected freedoms of action; they stress the absence of a fence rather than the presence of a guaranteed provision.
entries.definitionCN: 受保护的行动自由；它们强调没有栅栏，而不是有保障的供给。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin word for a human being, the Germanic word for a claim, real derived words and real international instruments.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「人」的词、日耳曼语中表示「主张」的词、真实派生词与真实的国际文书。

normal.en: The first half says species, the second says claim: a right you hold because you are human.
normal.cn: 前半说的是物种，后半说的是主张：一项因为你作为人而持有的权利。

normal.en: The family runs human, humane, humanity, humanitarian and inhuman.
normal.cn: 同族词包括「人的」、仁慈的、人类、人道主义的与无人性的。

normal.en: The catalogue splits into two generations: civil and political, then economic and social.
normal.cn: 这份清单分成两代：先是公民与政治权利，后是经济与社会权利。

normal.en: The phrase works even where no court will listen, because its ground is birth rather than statute.
normal.cn: 即使没有法院愿意受理，这个短语仍然有效，因为它的根据是出生，而不是法令。

normal.en: The 1948 declaration is the date most often attached to the modern phrase.
normal.cn: 1948 年的宣言是最常与现代这个短语联系在一起的年代。

abstract.en: Picture a door with no nameplate, opening for everyone who walks up to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有名牌的门，为每个走到它面前的人打开。

abstract.en: Picture a floor drawn under a battlefield, so that even the worst ground has a line beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象在战场之下画出的一层地板，使最糟的地面下面仍有一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a list that grows longer as people notice what they cannot do without.
abstract.cn: 想象一份清单，随着人们察觉自己缺什么就活不下去而不断变长。

examples.en: The court treated the detention as a violation of human rights.
examples.cn: 法院把这次拘押视为对人权的侵犯。

examples.en: Treaties on human rights often create monitoring bodies rather than direct remedies.
examples.cn: 人权条约往往设立监督机构，而不是直接提供救济。

examples.en: The argument over human rights is partly an argument over who may define them.
examples.cn: 关于人权的争论，有一部分是谁有权界定它们的争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「人+权」——先看前半的「人」，不分国籍与身份；再看后半的「权」，一张出生就带着、签不掉也拿不走的凭证。

root: human 出自拉丁语 humanus，源自 homo「人、人类」；homo 的更深来源有争议，与表示「土地」的词根相关的说法属假说，相关印欧语形式属重构形式。right 出自古英语 riht「直的、正当的」，属日耳曼语词，与拉丁语 rectus 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from one bare fact: being human. From that fact come inalienability and the international machinery that protects it; the catalogue then divides into civil and political on one side and economic and social on the other; wartime gives it a floor; moral use gives it a voice without a court; and the argument over universality gives it its sharpest criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个赤裸的事实长出：作为人。从这个事实分出不可让渡性，以及保护它的国际机器；清单随后分成一边的公民与政治权利、一边的经济与社会权利；战时给它一层底线；道义用法给它不必依赖法院的声音；而围绕普遍性的争论，则给了它最尖锐的批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nameless photograph that opens the same door for everyone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张没有名字的照片，为所有人打开同一扇门。

branches.en: BIRTHRIGHT: the claim that comes with birth, and the impossibility of signing it away.
branches.cn: 出生即有的权利：随出生而来的主张，以及把它签掉的不可行。

branches.en: LAW BEYOND BORDERS: treaties, courts and monitors that make the claim a matter between states.
branches.cn: 超越国界的法：使主张成为国家间事务的条约、法院与监督机构。

branches.en: TWO GENERATIONS: freedoms from restraint on one side, provision for a decent life on the other.
branches.cn: 两代人权：一边是免于约束的自由，一边是体面生活所需的供给。

branches.en: WARTIME FLOOR: the line that survives even where ordinary law has collapsed.
branches.cn: 战时底线：即便普通法律崩塌也仍然存在的那条线。

branches.en: CLAIM AND CONTEST: a moral appeal that needs no court, and the dispute over how wide it may reach.
branches.cn: 主张与争议：不需要法院的道义呼吁，以及关于它能伸展多宽的争论。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin adjective for the human species with a Germanic noun for a just claim. The derived family around the first half is large and has drifted toward kindness and collective existence.
intro.cn: 这个短语把表示人类物种的拉丁形容词与表示正当主张的日耳曼名词配在一起。前半周围的派生家族很大，并已漂向仁慈与整类存在。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below supply the human half of the phrase. The right half is Germanic; Latin has no borrowed form of it in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式提供短语中「人」的那一半。「权利」那一半属日耳曼语；这个家族中没有从拉丁语借入的对应形式。

items.meaning: entitlements held simply by being human
items.meaningCN: 仅因作为人而持有的应享之权
items.example: The report documented abuses of human rights.
items.exampleCN: 报告记录了侵犯人权的情形。

items.example: The fault was human rather than mechanical.
items.exampleCN: 过失在人而不在机械。

items.example: The shelter follows humane standards for animals.
items.exampleCN: 收容所遵循对待动物的人道标准。

items.meaning: all people; the quality of being humane
items.example: The discovery belongs to all humanity.
items.exampleCN: 这项发现属于全人类。

items.meaning: the branches of study concerned with human culture
items.meaningCN: 研究人类文化的诸学科
items.example: The university expanded its humanities faculty.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学扩充了人文学科。

items.example: A humanitarian corridor allowed civilians to leave.
items.exampleCN: 一条人道走廊让平民得以离开。

items.meaning: lacking the sympathy expected of people
items.example: The guards were accused of inhuman treatment.
items.exampleCN: 看守被指以无人性的方式对待人。

items.example: The memoir records the inhumanity of the camp.
items.exampleCN: 回忆录记录了营中的残忍。

items.example: Rescue workers showed superhuman endurance.
items.exampleCN: 救援人员表现出超常的耐力。

derivatives.zh: 人的；人类的（拉丁语中表示「人」的名词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，指属于人的）
人性；人类整体（形容词加表性质或集合的名词后缀，由个体属性转为整类存在）
人道主义的（形容词加表主义或从事者的后缀，指以减轻人的苦难为宗旨）
无人性的；残酷的（否定前缀加形容词，指缺少人应有的同情与节制）

definition_zh: 自由；自主；免除拘禁；免除某种负担的自由
definition_en: the condition of being free, able to act or speak as one chooses, or free from a particular burden or restraint
core_image: 一只笼门被打开，鸟没有立刻飞走，只站在门口，前路没有任何横杆
scene: 被释放的人走出监狱大门，抬头看见没有围墙的街道，第一次自己决定往哪边走。The released prisoner walked out of the gate under an open sky and for the first time chose his own direction in freedom.
sceneCN: 这里指「身体不再受拘禁、可以自行决定去向」，对应第 1 个义项：不被关押、不被束缚的行动状态；句意为被释放者走出大门，在开阔天空下第一次自行选择方向。画面要点：打开的笼门、没有围墙的街道、站在门口的人。

pos.zh: 自由；自主（不可数；表示具体各项自由时可用复数）

derivatives.zh: 自由的；不受奴役的（古英语形容词，指不属于奴隶身份，后扩展到不受任何约束）
自由地；自愿地（形容词加副词后缀，指不受限制地或以自愿方式）
自由民；荣誉市民（形容词与表示「人」的名词复合，指享有城市特权而非处于奴役身份的人）
不自由的（否定前缀加形容词，指处于被束缚或受强制状态）
热爱自由的（名词与表示「喜爱」的分词复合，指珍视不受强制的生活）

senses.title: Release from physical confinement
senses.definition: the condition of not being held prisoner, chained or otherwise physically restrained
senses.definitionCN: 不被囚禁、锁链束缚或以其他方式限制身体的状态
senses.example: The released prisoner walked out of the gate under an open sky and for the first time chose his own direction in freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 被释放的人走出大门，在开阔天空下第一次自由地选择方向。
senses.why: The oldest recorded sense is the opposite of slavery, so the word begins as a legal and bodily status before it becomes a philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早义项是奴隶身份的反面，因此这个词先是一种法律与身体上的身份，然后才成为哲学。

senses.title: Acting by one's own will
senses.definition: the ability to decide and act without being forced by another person
senses.definitionCN: 不受他人强制而自行决定与行动的能力
senses.example: Adults value the freedom to choose where they live.
senses.exampleCN: 成年人珍视选择居住地的自由。
senses.why: Once the body is unbound, the next question is who directs it, so the same word comes to name the absence of coercion.
senses.whyCN: 身体一旦解开束缚，接下来的问题就是谁来指挥它，于是同一个词开始命名「没有强制」的状态。

senses.title: Freedom to speak and publish
senses.definition: the right to express opinions and share information without punishment or censorship
senses.definitionCN: 不受惩罚或审查地表达意见、传播信息的权利
senses.example: The constitution protects freedom of expression.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法保护表达自由。
senses.why: Speech is the first thing a closed society restricts, so the abstract condition hardens into a named guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 言论是封闭社会最先限制的东西，因此这一抽象状态固化为一项有名字的保障。

senses.title: Freedom from want or fear
senses.definition: the condition of being relieved from a specific burden, such as hunger, threat or coercion
senses.definitionCN: 从某种特定负担（如饥饿、威胁或胁迫）中解脱出来的状态
senses.example: The charter promises freedom from fear as well as freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 宪章既承诺言论自由，也承诺免于恐惧。
senses.why: English allows the word to be followed by 'from', which turns a general condition into a list of particular burdens to be lifted.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个词后面接表示「脱离」的介词，从而把一般状态变成一张具体负担的清单。

senses.title: Self-rule of a people
senses.definition: the condition of a community governing itself instead of being ruled from outside
senses.definitionCN: 共同体自行治理、而非受外部统治的状态
senses.example: The colony celebrated its freedom after decades of foreign rule.
senses.exampleCN: 这块殖民地在数十年外来统治之后庆祝自己的自由。
senses.why: What applies to one body applies to a body politic, so the personal condition scales up to independence.
senses.whyCN: 适用于一个身体的，也适用于一个政治体，因此个人状态被放大为独立。

senses.title: Freedom of the will in philosophy
senses.definition: the disputed capacity of a person to choose otherwise than the causes acting on them would determine
senses.definitionCN: 人能否作出与作用其上的原因所决定的结果不同的选择，这一有争议的能力
senses.example: The debate over the freedom of the will has lasted for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 关于意志自由的争论已持续数百年。
senses.why: If action is not forced by another, philosophers ask whether it is determined at all, and the word is pushed to its most abstract limit.
senses.whyCN: 如果行动不被他人强制，哲学家就要问它是否仍被决定，于是这个词被推到最抽象的边界。

senses.title: Exemption from a duty
senses.definition: the state of not having to pay, perform or suffer something that others must
senses.definitionCN: 无须像他人那样支付、履行或承受某事的状态
senses.example: The treaty granted the port freedom from certain tolls.
senses.exampleCN: 条约给予该港口免除某些通行费的权利。
senses.why: A negative condition can attach to a single obligation, so freedom becomes a specific exemption written into a charter or contract.
senses.whyCN: 一种否定状态可以附着在单项义务上，于是自由变成写进宪章或合同的具体豁免。

senses.title: A granted latitude or privilege
senses.titleCN: 被给予的行动余地或特权
senses.definition: a permitted range of action, often granted by an authority to a person or a body
senses.definitionCN: 被允许的行动范围，常由权力机关授予个人或机构
senses.example: The curator was given the freedom of the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 馆长获得了自由使用档案的权限。
senses.why: The older sense of a civic privilege survives here: to have the freedom of a place is to be allowed to move through it as a member.
senses.whyCN: 市民特权这一较早的义项在此留存：拥有某地的自由，就是被允许以成员身份在其中行动。

intro.en: Freedom is a native English compound: the adjective free plus the suffix -dom, which comes from a word for judgment and jurisdiction. The Germanic adjective is reconstructed as a starred form, and its deepest origin is a hypothesis rather than a settled fact.
intro.cn: freedom 是英语本族复合词：形容词 free 加后缀 -dom，而该后缀出自一个表示「裁判、管辖」的词。这个日耳曼形容词的祖形以带星号的形式重构，其最深来源仍是假说，而非定论。

items.en: Freo meant 'free, not enslaved', and it could also describe a person who was noble or glad rather than servile.
items.cn: freo 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容人出身高贵或心情欢畅，而非卑屈。

items.en: Dom meant 'judgment, decree, jurisdiction', and as a suffix it built nouns for states, conditions and domains.
items.cn: dom 意为「裁判、法令、管辖」，作后缀时构成表示状态、境况与领域的名词。

items.en: Freodom joined the two and named the condition of one who is not enslaved; it could also mean a privilege or a charter of liberties.
items.cn: freodom 把两者结合，命名「不处于奴役状态」的境况；它也可指一项特权或一份自由特许状。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective is written with a star; Gothic freis and German frei are its recorded relatives. The starred form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 重构的形容词以带星号的形式书写；哥特语 freis 与德语 frei 是它的可考同族词。带星号的形式属重构形式，并非有文献实证的词。

items.en: A widely discussed hypothesis links the Germanic adjective to a root meaning 'to love', with Sanskrit priya 'beloved' as a distant relative. The link remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种流传较广的假说把这个日耳曼形容词与意为「爱」的词根相连，梵语 priya「亲爱的」是远亲。该联系仍属假说。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word also named a protected condition of citizens, and the plural freedoms came to mean specific guarantees. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个词也指公民受保护的状态，其复数形式后来指各项具体保障。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built from the same adjective or looks close to it; the second group offers near alternatives that stress different sides of not being constrained.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个形容词构成或与它形近；第二组是强调「不受约束」不同侧面的近义替代。

entries.definition: Not enslaved or not restricted; as a verb it means to release, so the same form covers the state and the act of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 不受奴役或不受限制；作动词时意为释放，因此同一形式既指状态，也指产生该状态的动作。

entries.definition: Without restriction, or willingly; it describes how an action is done rather than the condition itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不受限制地，或自愿地；它描述动作如何进行，而不是状态本身。

entries.definition: A person who is not a slave or who holds the privileges of a city; the compound names the holder, not the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 非奴隶身份或享有城市特权的人；这个复合词命名持有者，而不是状态。

entries.definition: Land held outright rather than rented; the word borrows the idea of not being bound, but applies it to tenure.
entries.definitionCN: 完全保有而非租用的土地；这个词借用了「不受束缚」的观念，但用于土地保有方式。

entries.definition: Freedom as a protected civil or political condition; it is more formal and often appears in legal and constitutional texts.
entries.definitionCN: 作为受保护的公民或政治状态的自由；它更正式，常出现在法律与宪法文本中。

entries.definition: The right or capacity of a person or group to govern itself; it stresses the source of the rules rather than the absence of a cage.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体自行治理的权利或能力；它强调规则的来源，而不是没有笼子。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is often used of nations and of people who support themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家，也用于自食其力的人。

entries.definition: The scope allowed for action or interpretation; it is a measured range rather than a principle.
entries.definitionCN: 被允许的行动或解释空间；它是被量出的范围，而不是一项原则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English adjective, the suffix for a condition, real derived words and real political phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语形容词、表状态的后缀、真实派生词与真实政治用语。

normal.en: The oldest sense is the opposite of slavery, so start from an unbound body rather than from a theory.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是奴隶身份的反面，因此从一具解开束缚的身体出发，而不是从理论出发。

normal.en: The suffix once meant judgment and jurisdiction, so a condition is something decreed over a domain.
normal.cn: 这个后缀原指裁判与管辖，因此「状态」是被施于某个领域之上的判定。

normal.en: The family runs free, freely, freeman, unfree and freedom-loving.
normal.cn: 同族词包括自由的、自由地、自由民、不自由的与热爱自由的。

normal.en: The phrase splits by preposition: freedom of speech, freedom from fear.
normal.cn: 这个短语按介词分流：言论的自由，免于恐惧的自由。

normal.en: A national flag and a personal choice use the same noun, which is why the political and private senses keep overlapping.
normal.cn: 一面国旗与一次个人选择用同一个名词，所以政治义与私人义不断重叠。

abstract.en: Picture an open cage with the door swung back and no lock visible anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一只打开的笼子，门被推开，哪里都看不到锁。

abstract.en: Picture a road with no fence on either side, but a sign at the entrance saying the traveller chooses the turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一条两侧没有栅栏的路，入口的牌子上写着由行路者自己选择转向。

abstract.en: Picture a map where a single person's unbound step becomes a whole nation's border.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，一个人解开束缚的一步，最终变成整个国家的边界。

examples.en: The law guarantees freedom of movement within the country.
examples.cn: 法律保障在本国境内行动的自由。

examples.en: Academic freedom protects scholars who challenge accepted views.
examples.cn: 学术自由保护挑战公认观点的学者。

examples.en: He gave up a well-paid post for the freedom to choose his own projects.
examples.cn: 他放弃了一份高薪职位，换取挑选自己课题的自由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗利多姆」——把「弗」听成「不」，把「多」听成「多出来的余地」：笼门一开，多出来的空间就是自由。

root: 古英语 freo「自由的、非奴隶的」+ 古英语 dom「裁判、法令、管辖」→ freodom。该形容词的日耳曼语祖形属重构形式（*frijaz），哥特语 freis、德语 frei 为可考同族词；更深来源有「爱」词根的假说，未成定论。这个词族没有拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings begin with an unbound body. From there the word asks who directs the body, which yields free action; it then names specific guarantees of speech, exemptions from hunger and fear, the self-rule of a people, the philosophical question of the will, and the older civic privilege of moving through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具解开束缚的身体开始。随后这个词追问谁来指挥这具身体，于是有了自主行动；它又命名言论的具体保障、免于饥饿与恐惧的豁免、民族的自治、关于意志的哲学问题，以及较早的、可在某地自由行动的市民特权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an opened cage with no bar across the way out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只被打开的笼子，出口处没有任何横杆。

branches.en: NO CAGE: the bodily and legal core, release from confinement or slavery.
branches.cn: 没有笼子：身体与法律的内核，从拘禁或奴役中释放。

branches.en: OWN WILL: acting without coercion, and the narrower case of being exempt from one duty.
branches.cn: 自己的意志：不受强制地行动，以及免除某一项义务这一较窄情形。

branches.en: OPEN SPEECH: the first guarantee that a closed society takes away.
branches.cn: 开放的言说：封闭社会最先夺走的那项保障。

branches.en: FREE FROM: release from hunger and fear, and the philosophical puzzle of an undetermined will.
branches.cn: 免于：从饥饿与恐惧中解脱，以及意志是否被决定的哲学难题。

branches.en: SELF-RULE AND LATITUDE: a people governing itself, and the granted room to move within a place.
branches.cn: 自治与余地：一个民族自行治理，以及在某地获准的行动空间。

intro.en: The word is a Germanic compound: an adjective for not being enslaved plus a suffix that once meant judgment and jurisdiction. No Latin element belongs to this family.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语复合词：一个表示「不受奴役」的形容词，加上一个原意为「裁判与管辖」的后缀。这个家族没有拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family; its recorded relatives are Germanic. Latin-derived near synonyms such as liberty come from a different root altogether.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有拉丁语来源，其可考同族词都属日耳曼语。由拉丁语派生的近义词如「自由权」出自完全不同的词根。

items.meaning: the condition of not being bound
items.example: The gate opened and the prisoner tasted freedom.
items.exampleCN: 大门打开，囚犯尝到了自由的滋味。

items.meaningCN: 不受奴役的；不受限制的
items.example: The former slave was a free man at last.
items.exampleCN: 从前的奴隶终于成了自由人。

items.example: Members may speak freely at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 成员可在会上自由发言。

items.example: The freeman voted in the guild election.
items.exampleCN: 这位自由民在行会选举中投票。

items.example: Only free-born citizens could hold the office.
items.exampleCN: 只有生而自由的公民才能担任该职。

items.example: The workers were unfree in all but name.
items.exampleCN: 这些工人名义之外处处不自由。

items.meaning: one who fights for national or civil freedom
items.meaningCN: 为民族或公民自由而战的人
items.example: The monument honours the freedom fighters.
items.exampleCN: 纪念碑纪念那些自由战士。

items.example: The old kingdom fell in a single season.
items.exampleCN: 那个古王国在一个季节里覆灭。

items.example: Her wisdom came from long experience.
items.exampleCN: 她的智慧来自长期经验。

自由地；自愿地（形容词加副词后缀，指不受限制地或以自愿方式）
自由民；荣誉市民（形容词与表示「人」的名词复合，指享有城市特权而非处于奴役身份的人）
不自由的（否定前缀加形容词，指处于被束缚或受强制状态）

definition_zh: 自由；自由权；擅自；获准行动的范围
definition_en: freedom to live and act as one chooses, especially as a condition protected by law or constitution
core_image: 一根被砸断的锁链落在石阶上，锁孔里还插着半截钥匙，人已经走远
scene: 城邦的公民在广场上宣读宪章，声称任何人不得未经审判而被拘押。Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
sceneCN: 这里指「受法律保障、不受任意拘押的个人自由」，对应第 1 个义项：法律保护的、免于任意逮捕的自由；句意为公民宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人。画面要点：广场、宪章、砸断的锁链。

pos.zh: 自由；自由权（不可数；表示各项具体自由时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 获准的；自由的；有空闲的

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽容的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的、宽厚的」形容词经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

senses.title: Protection from arbitrary detention
senses.titleCN: 免于任意拘押的个人自由
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot be arrested or held except by lawful procedure
senses.definitionCN: 除依法定程序外不得被逮捕或拘押的个人状态
senses.example: Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在广场宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人，这是对个人自由的保障。
senses.why: In Roman law the free person's body could not be seized at will, so liberty begins as a legal status rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，自由人的身体不能被随意捉拿，因此「自由」一开始是一种法律身份，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Self-government of a community
senses.definition: the condition of a city or people that makes its own laws instead of receiving them from a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 城市或民族自行立法、而不是从统治者那里接受法律的状态
senses.example: The city kept its liberties against the duke for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城邦两代人以来一直保有对抗公爵的自由权。
senses.why: Medieval towns bought charters that listed their liberties, so the word came to name a body's collective self-rule.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪城镇买下特许状，状上逐条列出它们的自由权，于是这个词也命名一个群体的自治。

senses.title: Specific rights protected by law
senses.titleCN: 法律保护的各项具体自由权
senses.definition: the several freedoms, such as speech, worship and assembly, that a constitution or statute guarantees
senses.definitionCN: 宪法或法律所保障的若干项自由，如言论、礼拜与集会
senses.example: The bill lists the liberties that the state may not remove.
senses.exampleCN: 权利法案列出了国家不得取消的各项自由。
senses.why: The abstract condition becomes countable when each guarantee is written down separately, which is why the plural is so common in legal texts.
senses.whyCN: 当每一项保障被分别写下来，抽象状态就变得可数，这就是复数形式在法律文本中如此常见的原因。

senses.title: Overstepping what is allowed
senses.definition: the act of acting beyond one's permitted scope, especially in a way that is presumptuous
senses.definitionCN: 超出自己被允许的范围行事，尤指冒失无礼地这样做
senses.example: The visitor took liberties with the archive and rearranged the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那位访客擅自摆弄档案，把文件重新排列了。
senses.why: A granted latitude can be used too far, so the same noun turns ironic and names the abuse of a permission.
senses.whyCN: 获准的余地可能被用过了头，于是同一个名词转为反讽，命名对许可的滥用。

senses.title: Being permitted or free to act
senses.definition: the state of being allowed to do something, or of being free from obligation at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 获准做某事、或在某一时刻没有义务在身的状态
senses.example: You are at liberty to inspect the records yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以自行查阅这些记录。
senses.why: The phrase 'at liberty' keeps the old legal sense of a person not under restraint, and from it comes the polite formula for permission.
senses.whyCN: 「处于自由状态」这一短语保留了「人未受拘束」的旧法律义，礼貌的许可说法正是从这里来的。

senses.title: Freedom of conscience and worship
senses.definition: the right to hold and practise a faith without state pressure
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家压力地持有并实践信仰的权利
senses.example: Religious liberty was the first liberty to be argued for in print.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由是最早被以印刷文字论证的自由。
senses.why: Where the state and the church were the same body, the demand to worship otherwise was the sharpest test of a protected sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当国家与教会合为一体，要求以别的方式礼拜，就成了对「受保护领域」最尖锐的检验。

senses.title: Freedom of the will
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that a person can choose without being wholly determined by prior causes
senses.definitionCN: 人能够作出选择、而不完全被先在原因所决定的哲学主张
senses.example: The essay asks whether liberty of the will survives a strict causal account.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章追问，在严格的决定论解释下，意志自由是否还能成立。
senses.why: Once legal restraint is removed, the remaining question is whether anything else restrains the will, and the word follows the question inward.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律约束被移除，剩下的问题就是是否有别的东西在约束意志，这个词便随问题向内走。

senses.title: The range of a granted freedom
senses.definition: the extent of a place or body of knowledge that a person is allowed to use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人被允许使用的场所或知识范围
senses.example: The scholar was given the liberty of the whole collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者获准自由使用全部藏书。
senses.why: To have the liberty of a place is an old civic formula: not ownership, but the permitted run of it.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有某地的自由」是一个古老的市民说法：不是所有权，而是被允许在其中往来。

intro.en: Liberty comes from Latin libertas, the condition of a free person, built on liber 'free'. The deeper origin of liber is uncertain. English took the word through Old French, and its plural came to mean specific chartered privileges.
intro.cn: liberty 出自拉丁语 libertas，指自由人的身份，建立在 liber「自由的」之上。liber 的更深来源不确定。英语经古法语吸收此词，其复数后来指特许状上具体列明的特权。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not a slave' and could also describe a person of noble or generous status. Its own origin is uncertain; a connection with a root meaning 'to grow' has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容出身高贵或气度宽厚的人。它本身的来源不确定；有人提出它与意为「生长」的词根相关，但未获确立。

items.en: Libertas named the condition of a free person and, in Roman public life, the status that law protected against arbitrary seizure.
items.cn: libertas 指自由人的身份；在罗马公共生活中，它指法律保护、免于任意捉拿的身份。

items.en: Old French liberte carried the noun into English, at first in religious and civic contexts rather than in philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语 liberte 把这个名词带入英语，最初用于宗教与市民语境，而不是哲学。

items.en: Towns and guilds listed their liberties in charters, and the plural became a name for specific privileges held by a body.
items.cn: 城镇与行会在特许状中逐条列出自己的自由权，其复数形式于是成为某个群体所持具体特权的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the singular named a general political condition, and documents began to speak of civil liberty. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，单数形式指一般的政治状态，文书开始谈论公民自由。年代为约数。

items.en: The same noun was applied to the will, producing the long debate over liberty of the will that continues in philosophy.
items.cn: 同一个名词被用到意志上，产生了关于意志自由的长期争论，这一争论在哲学中延续至今。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective or looks deceptively close to it, including one word whose Latin source is a different noun altogether; the second group gives near alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个拉丁形容词构成或与它形近得容易误认，其中还有一个词的拉丁来源是另一个名词；第二组是近义替代。

entries.definition: Generous or open-minded, and in politics favourable to reform; it began as 'of a free person' and moved toward generosity of attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、开明的，政治上倾向改革；它起初意为「自由人的」，后来转向态度上的宽宏。

entries.definition: To set a person or place free from control; it names the act that produces liberty rather than the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或地方脱离控制；它命名产生自由的动作，而不是状态。

entries.definition: A place where books are kept; its Latin source is a word for a book or the bark used for writing, not the adjective for freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书之所；它的拉丁来源是表示「书」或书写用树皮的词，而不是表示自由的形容词。

entries.definition: A published false statement that harms a reputation; it comes from a small Latin book or booklet, with no link to freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与自由无关。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being bound; it covers body, will and speech, while liberty more often names a legally protected status.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚的一般状态；它覆盖身体、意志与言论，而本词更常指受法律保护的身份。

entries.definition: The right of a person or region to govern itself; it stresses who makes the rules rather than what is forbidden.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或地区自行治理的权利；它强调由谁制定规则，而不是禁止什么。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is common for nations and for self-supporting people.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家与自食其力的人。

entries.definition: An official permission to do something; it is narrower than liberty because it is granted case by case and can be revoked.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方许可；它比自由窄，因为逐案授予且可被撤回。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for a free person, real derived words and real legal formulas, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示自由人的形容词、真实派生词与真实法律套语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a legal status: a free body that cannot be seized at will.
normal.cn: 核心是一种法律身份：一具不能被随意捉拿的自由身体。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberate, liberation and libertarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括宽厚的、解放、解放过程与自由意志论者。

normal.en: Medieval towns kept their liberties in written charters, which is why the plural means specific privileges.
normal.cn: 中世纪城镇把自由权写进特许状，所以复数形式指具体特权。

normal.en: The phrase at liberty means both free from restraint and free to act.
normal.cn: 「处于自由状态」这一说法既指不受拘束，也指可以行动。

normal.en: Taking liberties is the ironic side: using a permission further than it was given.
normal.cn: 「擅自」是这个词的反讽一面：把许可用得比给予的更远。

abstract.en: Picture a broken chain on a step with the key still in the lock, and the person already out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上一根断链，钥匙还插在锁里，人已经走远。

abstract.en: Picture a charter rolled open on a town table, each paragraph a named freedom.
abstract.cn: 想象城镇桌上一卷摊开的特许状，每一段都是一项有名字的自由。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked permission that opens only when the right name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「许可」的门，只有说出正确的名分才会打开。

examples.en: The court held that the detention violated his liberty.
examples.cn: 法院认定这次拘押侵犯了他的自由。

examples.en: You are at liberty to leave whenever you wish.
examples.cn: 你随时都可以离开。

examples.en: The reporter took liberties with the quotation and changed its sense.
examples.cn: 那名记者擅自改动引文，改变了它的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离不体」——身体离开束缚，就不必再贴着锁链过日子；自由就是能走开的那一步。

root: 拉丁语 liber「自由的、非奴隶的」→ libertas「自由人的身份」→ 经古法语 liberte 进入英语。liber 的更深来源不确定，与意为「生长」的词根相关的说法属假说；同族的 liberalis 意为「自由人的、宽厚的」，是另一条语义支线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a free body that the law may not seize. From that status come self-rule for a community, the list of named guarantees, the permission formula, the ironic overstepping of permission, the freedom of worship, the philosophical liberty of the will, and the old civic right to move through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具法律不得随意捉拿的自由身体开始。从这个身份分出共同体的自治、逐条列名的保障、许可的说法、对许可的反讽式越界、信仰的自由、哲学上的意志自由，以及古老的、可在某地往来的市民权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain broken at the link, with the key still turning in the lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：链环被砸断的锁链，钥匙还在锁里转动。

branches.en: UNBOUND BODY: protection from arbitrary arrest, and the polite formula that a person is free to act.
branches.cn: 不受束缚的身体：免于任意逮捕，以及「可以自由行动」的礼貌说法。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a town or people that makes its own law.
branches.cn: 自治：自行立法的城镇或民族。

branches.en: NAMED GUARANTEES: the several liberties written in a charter, and the permitted run of a place.
branches.cn: 列名的保障：写进特许状的各项自由，以及在某地获准走动的范围。

branches.en: OVERSTEPPING: the same permission used beyond what was granted.
branches.cn: 越界：同一份许可被用得超出所给予的范围。

branches.en: CONSCIENCE AND WILL: worship without pressure, and the inner question of whether the will is determined.
branches.cn: 良心与意志：不受压力的礼拜，以及意志是否被决定的内在问题。

intro.en: The whole family rests on one Latin adjective for a free person, with noun, verb and agent endings added over time; the Germanic near synonym freedom belongs to a separate history.
intro.cn: 整个家族都依托一个表示自由人的拉丁形容词，随后加上名词、动词与施事后缀；日耳曼语的近义词「自由」属于另一段历史。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the derived adjective for generosity of character.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及由它派生、表示气度宽厚的形容词。

items.meaning: the condition of a free person
items.example: The charter guaranteed the liberty of every citizen.
items.exampleCN: 宪章保障每位公民的自由。

items.meaning: of a free person; generous, open-minded
items.meaningCN: 自由人的；宽厚的、开明的
items.example: A liberal education once meant the studies fit for a free person.
items.exampleCN: 「自由教育」原指适合自由人研习的科目。

items.meaningCN: 宽厚，尤指态度上的宽容
items.example: The host was praised for his liberality.
items.exampleCN: 主人因宽厚而受到称赞。

items.example: The troops liberated the occupied town.
items.exampleCN: 部队解放了被占领的城镇。

items.example: The museum marks the anniversary of the liberation.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆纪念解放周年。

items.example: The general was hailed as a liberator.
items.exampleCN: 那位将军被称颂为解放者。

items.meaning: one who holds personal freedom to be the highest value
items.meaningCN: 主张个人自由至上的人
items.example: The candidate described himself as a libertarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位候选人自称自由意志论者。

items.example: The measure was criticised as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The villagers gave thanks for their deliverance.
items.exampleCN: 村民们为获救而致谢。

latinEntries.meaning: freedom; the status of a free person
