derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽厚的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的」形容词加形容词后缀，经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

definition_zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于遭受的；很可能发生的
definition_en: legally responsible for something, or likely to do or suffer something
core_image: 一根绳子把签了名的契约系在一只脚踝上，另一头连着一块写着「赔偿」的木牌
scene: 保险公司在条款中写明，运输途中货物受损时由承运人承担赔偿。The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
sceneCN: 这里指「依法对某项损害承担赔偿」，对应第 1 个义项：因契约或法律而被绑定、必须负责；句意为条款规定运输途中货物受损由承运人负责。画面要点：签名的契约、系在脚踝上的绳、写着「赔偿」的木牌。

pos.zh: 有法律责任的；负有义务的；易于…的；很可能…的（多作表语，后接表示对象或方向的介词）

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
有限责任（形容词与名词构成的复合术语，指以出资额为限的责任形式）

senses.title: Legally answerable for damage
senses.titleCN: 对损害依法负有赔偿责任
senses.definition: bound by law or contract to pay for loss or injury one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 依法或依契约必须为自己造成的损失或伤害作出赔偿
senses.example: The policy states that the carrier is liable for damage to the goods while they are in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 条款规定，运输途中货物受损由承运人负责赔偿。
senses.why: The word began as 'able to be bound', and a contract is exactly the rope that binds a party to answer for a loss.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初意为「可被绑住的」，而契约正是那根把一方绑住、使其对损失负责的绳子。

senses.title: Answerable for a debt
senses.definition: obliged to settle a debt or to perform an undertaking, often because one has guaranteed it
senses.definitionCN: 必须清偿债务或履行承诺，常因本人曾为之作保
senses.example: A guarantor is liable for the loan if the borrower defaults.
senses.exampleCN: 借款人违约时，担保人对该笔贷款负有责任。
senses.why: Money makes the bond visible: the rope now runs to a specific sum that must be paid.
senses.whyCN: 金钱让这根绳子看得见：它现在连着一个必须偿付的具体数额。

senses.title: Subject to a penalty or a charge
senses.definition: exposed by law to a fine, a tax or some other imposed charge
senses.definitionCN: 依法可能被课以罚款、税款或其他征收
senses.example: Income above that threshold is liable to tax.
senses.exampleCN: 超过该门槛的收入应纳税。
senses.why: The bond can run toward an authority rather than a victim, so the same word covers what the state may exact.
senses.whyCN: 这根绳子也可以通向权力机关而不是受害者，因此同一个词也覆盖国家可以征收的部分。

senses.title: Exposed to harm
senses.definition: open to a particular risk, such as injury, loss or damage, because of circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 因所处情况而暴露于某种风险，如受伤、损失或损坏
senses.example: Low-lying fields are liable to flooding in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 低洼的田地在春天容易遭水淹。
senses.why: From 'bound to answer' the word loosens into 'open to', a shift from a legal tie to a physical exposure.
senses.whyCN: 从「必须负责」松弛为「暴露于」，这是从法律束缚向身体处境的转移。

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: probable, especially of something unwelcome that may occur
senses.definitionCN: 很可能发生，尤指可能发生的不快之事
senses.example: The bridge is liable to close when the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 风一大，这座桥就可能关闭。
senses.why: If a thing is exposed to a risk, it will often meet it, so exposure slides into probability.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物暴露于某种风险，它往往会遇上，于是「暴露」滑向「概率」。

senses.title: Prone to do something
senses.definition: having a tendency to act in a certain way, often unintentionally or regrettably
senses.definitionCN: 有以某种方式行事的倾向，常指无意或令人遗憾的行为
senses.example: He is liable to forget names under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 他在压力之下容易忘记名字。
senses.why: A person can be bound to an outcome by his own habits, so the word moves from outer obligation to inner tendency.
senses.whyCN: 人可能被自己的习惯绑向某个结果，因此这个词从外在义务移向内在倾向。

senses.title: Obliged to serve
senses.titleCN: 有义务服役或尽某项义务
senses.definition: required by law to perform a service, such as military duty or statutory work
senses.definitionCN: 依法须履行某项服务，如兵役或法定工作
senses.example: All men of that age were liable for military service.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年龄的所有男子都有服兵役的义务。
senses.why: The bond here is to the state and to a duty rather than to a creditor, but the grammar of being bound is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的绳子通向国家与一项义务，而不是通向债权人，但「被绑住」的语法没有变。

senses.title: Mildly probable in speech
senses.definition: used informally to mean that something may well happen, with less force than a prediction
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示某事很可能发生，语气比预测更弱
senses.example: She is liable to be late if the traffic is bad.
senses.exampleCN: 如果交通不好，她可能会迟到。
senses.why: In everyday speech the legal weight drains away, leaving only a softened forecast that keeps a trace of the old 'bound to happen'.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语中，法律分量被抽走，只剩一个软化的预测，仍留着「注定会发生」的一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Liable comes from Old French lier 'to bind', from Latin ligare, with the adjective ending -able. It first meant 'able to be bound', then 'bound by law to answer', and later widened to exposure and probability.
intro.cn: liable 出自古法语 lier「捆绑」，源头为拉丁语 ligare，加上形容词后缀 -able。它最初意为「可被绑住的」，继而指「依法须负责的」，后扩展到「暴露于」与「很可能」。

items.en: Ligare 'to bind' is the verb behind the word; the same root also produced alliance, obligation and ligament.
items.cn: ligare 意为「捆绑」，是这个词背后的动词；同一词根还产生了「联盟」「义务」与「韧带」。

items.en: Old French lier carried the verb into English, and its participle gave the sense of something or someone bound.
items.cn: 古法语 lier 把这个动词带入英语，其分词给出「被绑住的」这一意思。

items.en: The adjective formed with the ending for 'able' meant 'able to be bound', at first in the sense of being bound by law to answer for something.
items.cn: 加上表示「可…的」后缀构成的形容词，意为「可被绑住的」，最初指依法须对某事负责。

items.en: In medieval and early modern law the word described a person bound to pay or to answer, and fixed phrases named the object of the bond.
items.cn: 在中世纪与近代早期的法律中，这个词描述被绑定须付款或须作答的人，固定搭配则指明被绑向的对象。

items.en: The widening from 'bound to answer' to 'exposed to' and then to 'likely to' happened gradually, and the first date of the looser use is uncertain.
items.cn: 从「必须负责」扩展到「暴露于」再到「很可能」，这一过程是渐进的，较松弛用法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound close but come from other sources or carry other senses; the second group gives near alternatives for responsibility and for proneness.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但来源不同或另有含义的词；第二组是「责任」与「易于」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: A published false statement that damages a reputation; it comes from a Latin word for a small book, not from the verb to bind.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与「捆绑」无关。

entries.definition: Able to be trusted; it is formed from the verb rely plus the same ending, and has nothing to do with legal responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可信赖的；它由动词「依赖」加同一个后缀构成，与法律责任无关。

entries.definition: Unstable or easily changed, used in chemistry and psychology; its Latin source means 'sliding', not 'binding'.
entries.definitionCN: 不稳定、易变的，用于化学与心理学；它的拉丁来源意为「滑动」，而不是「捆绑」。

entries.definition: Having a duty to deal with something and being answerable for it; it is wider than the entry word and need not be legal.
entries.definitionCN: 有义务处理某事并须为之负责；它比本词宽，而且不必是法律上的。

entries.definition: Required to explain or justify one's actions to a person or body; it stresses reporting upward rather than paying for loss.
entries.definitionCN: 须向某人或机构解释、交代自己的行为；它强调向上报告，而不是赔偿损失。

entries.definition: Likely to suffer from or to do something, usually something bad; it covers the exposure sense but carries no legal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 易遭受或易做出某事，通常是不好的事；它覆盖「暴露」这一义，却不带法律义务。

entries.definition: Likely to do something, often in a neutral or habitual way; it lacks the sense of risk that the entry word usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，常为中性的或习惯性的；它缺少本词通常带的「风险」意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb to bind, the adjective ending for 'able', real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「捆绑」的动词、表示「可…的」形容词后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a rope: liable means able to be bound, and a contract is the rope.
normal.cn: 核心是一根绳子：本词意为「可被绑住的」，而契约就是那根绳。

normal.en: The family runs liability, liabilities and limited liability.
normal.cn: 同族词包括责任、各项债务与有限责任。

normal.en: The preposition sorts the senses: liable for a loss, liable to a penalty or a flood.
normal.cn: 介词把义项分开：对损失负责，应受处罚或易遭水淹。

normal.en: The same root appears in alliance, obligation and ligament, all forms of binding.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在联盟、义务与韧带中，都是不同形式的「绑」。

normal.en: In speech the legal rope goes slack, and liable becomes a soft way of saying likely.
normal.cn: 在口语中法律之绳松脱，这个词变成「很可能」的软说法。

abstract.en: Picture a signed paper tied to an ankle, so that wherever the person walks the obligation follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张签了名的纸系在脚踝上，人走到哪里，义务就跟到哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a field lying low beside a river, exposed each spring without anyone having agreed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象河边的低洼田地，每年春天都被淹，而没有任何人同意过这件事。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that slowly turns into a probability, still tied but no longer pulled by a court.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子慢慢变成一种概率，仍然系着，却不再被法庭拉动。

examples.en: The manufacturer is liable for defects found within two years.
examples.cn: 制造商对两年内发现的缺陷负有责任。

examples.en: Drivers are liable to heavy fines for using a phone at the wheel.
examples.cn: 司机开车时使用电话可能被重罚。

examples.en: The old roof is liable to leak after a long storm.
examples.cn: 旧屋顶在长时间暴雨之后容易漏水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖不了的」——签了字就得赔，绳子系在脚上，赖也赖不掉，所以是有责任的。

root: 古法语 lier「捆绑」← 拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」→ 加表示「可…的」后缀构成 liable，字面为「可被绑住的」。ligare 的更深来源一般认为是印欧语中表示「系、缠」的词根，相关形式属重构形式；同根词包括 alliance、obligation、ligament。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings unwind from one rope. Bound by a contract gives legal responsibility and debts; bound toward an authority gives penalties, taxes and service; loosening the rope gives exposure to harm, then likelihood and personal tendency; and in casual speech the rope nearly disappears, leaving only a soft forecast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一根绳子解开。被契约绑住，产生法律责任与债务；被绑向权力机关，产生处罚、税款与服役义务；绳子一松，产生暴露于损害、可能性与个人倾向；到了口语里绳子几乎消失，只剩一个软化的预测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed obligation tied to the ankle, following the person wherever he goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在脚踝上的签名义务，人走到哪里它就跟到哪里。

branches.en: BOUND: legal answerability for damage, and the duty to settle a debt.
branches.cn: 被绑住：对损害的依法负责，以及清偿债务的义务。

branches.en: OWED TO AUTHORITY: penalties and taxes on one side, service to the state on the other.
branches.cn: 欠向权力：一边是处罚与税款，一边是对国家的服役义务。

branches.en: EXPOSED: open to injury, loss or damage because of where one stands.
branches.cn: 暴露：因所处位置而易于受伤、受损或遭损失。

branches.en: LIKELY AND PRONE: what probably happens, and what a person tends to do.
branches.cn: 可能与倾向：很可能发生的事，以及一个人容易做出的举动。

branches.en: LOOSE FORECAST: the everyday weakening of the word into a mild 'may well'.
branches.cn: 松脱的预测：日常用法中弱化为轻微的「很可能」。

intro.en: One Latin verb for binding underlies the word and a large neighbouring family; the adjective ending adds the idea of capacity, and later endings build nouns and verbs for obligations.
intro.cn: 一个表示「捆绑」的拉丁动词支撑着这个词与一大片相邻词族；形容词后缀加上「能力」之意，后来的后缀又构成表示义务的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the verb of binding and its compounds; the English words built on them keep the same physical image of a tie.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示表示「捆绑」的动词及其复合形式；由它们构成的英语词都保留同一种「系绑」的实体意象。

items.meaning: able to be bound, hence answerable
items.meaningCN: 可被绑住的，因而须负责的
items.example: The carrier is liable for the loss.
items.exampleCN: 承运人对该损失负有责任。

items.example: The firm accepted liability for the accident.
items.exampleCN: 公司承认对该事故负有责任。

items.meaning: debts shown on a balance sheet
items.meaningCN: 资产负债表上列出的各项债务
items.example: The company's liabilities exceeded its assets.
items.exampleCN: 公司的债务超过了资产。

items.example: The two states allied against the fleet.
items.exampleCN: 两国结盟对抗那支舰队。

items.meaningCN: 依协议形成的正式联合
items.example: The alliance held through the winter.
items.exampleCN: 这个联盟维持了整个冬天。

items.meaning: to bind someone by duty or favour
items.meaningCN: 以义务或恩惠约束某人
items.example: The contract obliges the seller to deliver.
items.exampleCN: 合同使卖方负有交付义务。

items.meaning: a duty one is bound to perform
items.example: The lease sets out the tenant's obligations.
items.exampleCN: 租约列明了租户的义务。

items.meaning: a band that binds bones together
items.meaningCN: 把骨骼系连起来的韧带
items.example: The runner tore a ligament in his knee.
items.exampleCN: 跑者撕裂了膝部的一条韧带。

items.meaning: a tie or band, also joined letters
items.example: The surgeon applied a ligature to the vessel.
items.exampleCN: 外科医生用系带结扎了那条血管。

latinEntries.meaning: to bind, to put under obligation

derivatives.zh: 责任；债务（形容词加表性质的名词后缀，由「可被约束的」转为「须承担的法律责任」）
各项债务（名词加复数词尾，指账面上须偿付的多项义务）
义务（由同根的「使受约束」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指必须履行的事）
联盟（由同根的「系到一处」动词加表行为的名词后缀构成，指依协议形成的联合）

definition_en: the branch of law governing agreements that courts will enforce, including how they are formed, read and remedied
core_image: 两份对折的契约并排摊开，中间压着一枚印章，边缘用一条细线把双方连成一份可执行的义务
scene: 法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课，学生先学契约如何成立。The law school teaches offer, acceptance and remedies for breach as one course, so students first learn how contracts are formed under contract law.
sceneCN: 这里指「规范合同成立、解释与救济的法律部门」，对应第 1 个义项：关于契约的整体规则体系；句意为法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课。画面要点：两份摊开的契约、中间的印章、连接双方的细线。

pos.zh: 合同法；契约法（不可数，作学科或法律部门名称）

derivatives.zh: 合同的；契约上的（名词加形容词后缀，指由合同约定或与合同有关的）
依合同地（形容词加副词后缀，指以合同条款为依据）
承包人；订约方（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指承接工程或服务的一方）
收缩；缩略（动词加表行为的名词后缀，语义由「拉到一起」转为「体积变小」或「词形缩短」）

senses.title: The branch governing enforceable agreements
senses.titleCN: 规范可执行协议的法律部门
senses.definition: the body of rules that decides which promises the law will enforce and what happens when they are broken
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些承诺法律会强制执行、以及承诺被违反时如何处理的那套规则
senses.example: The law school teaches offer, acceptance and remedies for breach as one course, so students first learn how contracts are formed under contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 法学院把要约、承诺与违约救济编成一门课，学生先学合同法下契约如何成立。
senses.why: The phrase joins a word for drawing two parties into one bond with a word for laid-down rules, so the subject is the rules of that bond.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示「把双方拉到一起」的词与表示「被定下的规则」的词连在一起，因此这门学科就是那种绑定的规则。

senses.title: How an agreement comes into being
senses.definition: the rules on offer and acceptance, and on the moment at which a binding agreement arises
senses.definitionCN: 关于要约与承诺、以及有约束力的协议在何时产生的规则
senses.example: A contract is formed when acceptance reaches the offeror.
senses.exampleCN: 承诺到达要约人时，合同即告成立。
senses.why: A bond needs two hands to tie it, so the subject begins with the exchange that turns two intentions into one obligation.
senses.whyCN: 一根绳子需要两只手来系，因此这门学科从那个把两个意图变成一个义务的交换开始。

senses.title: Consideration and cause
senses.definition: the requirement that each side give something in exchange, so that a promise is not a bare gift
senses.definitionCN: 要求双方各给出某种交换物，使承诺不只是一份空手赠予
senses.example: A promise without consideration is generally not enforceable in that system.
senses.exampleCN: 在该法系中，没有对价的承诺一般不可强制执行。
senses.why: Law will not bind a person who received nothing, so the doctrine asks what each hand put into the knot.
senses.whyCN: 法律不愿绑住一个什么也没得到的人，因此这一学说追问每只手在绳结里放了什么。

senses.title: Reading the words of the agreement
senses.definition: the rules courts use to decide what the words of a contract mean when the parties disagree
senses.definitionCN: 当事人发生分歧时，法院用来判定合同文字含义的规则
senses.example: The court applied the ordinary meaning rule of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 法院适用了合同法中的通常含义规则。
senses.why: Once a bond is written, its words can be pulled in two directions, and the subject must supply a method for reading them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦绳子被写成文字，文字就可能被往两个方向拉扯，这门学科必须提供一种读法。

senses.title: Breach and the remedy
senses.definition: the rules on what counts as breaking a promise and what the injured party may recover
senses.definitionCN: 关于什么构成违反承诺、以及受害方可以取得何种补偿的规则
senses.example: Damages are the usual remedy for breach under contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 在合同法下，损害赔偿是违约的通常救济。
senses.why: A tie that cannot be broken without consequence is what makes the bond real, so remedy is the enforcement half of the subject.
senses.whyCN: 一根被扯断就要承担后果的绳子，才使绑缚成为真实，因此救济是这门学科的强制执行那一半。

senses.title: Defences that undo the bond
senses.definition: grounds such as fraud, duress, mistake or incapacity on which a party may escape the agreement
senses.definitionCN: 欺诈、胁迫、错误或无行为能力等理由，当事人可据此脱离协议
senses.example: Duress is a defence that removes the contract altogether.
senses.exampleCN: 胁迫是一种使合同整体失效的抗辩。
senses.why: A bond tied by a hand that was forced or deceived was not freely tied, so the subject must provide ways to untie it.
senses.whyCN: 被强迫或被欺骗的手系出的绳结并非自由系成，因此这门学科必须提供解开它的方式。

senses.title: Form and formalities
senses.definition: the cases in which writing, signature, seal or registration is required before an agreement binds
senses.definitionCN: 在哪些情形下协议须有书面、签名、盖章或登记才产生约束力
senses.example: Some sales require a written record as a formality of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 某些买卖依合同法的形式要求须有书面记录。
senses.why: Some ties must be made in public to be trusted, so the subject keeps a list of knots that need witnesses or paper.
senses.whyCN: 有些绳结必须在人前系成才可信，因此这门学科保留了一份需要见证人或纸面的清单。

senses.title: Rules across borders
senses.definition: the international conventions and standard terms that govern agreements between parties in different countries
senses.definitionCN: 管束不同国家当事人之间协议的国际公约与标准条款
senses.example: Two firms in different states may choose a convention of contract law.
senses.exampleCN: 分处两国的两家公司可以选择适用某项合同公约。
senses.why: Trade crosses borders faster than legislatures write rules, so the subject acquires an international layer of agreed texts.
senses.whyCN: 贸易跨过国界的速度快于立法者写规则的速度，因此这门学科获得了一层国际商定的文本。

intro.en: Contract descends from Latin contrahere 'to draw together', built on trahere 'to draw'. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', not from Latin. The compound is a modern name for a branch of private law.
intro.cn: contract 出自拉丁语 contrahere「拉到一起」，建立在 trahere「拉」之上。law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，并非来自拉丁语。这个复合词是近代私法部门的名称。

items.en: Trahere 'to draw, pull' is the verb inside the word; the same root also underlies extract, attract and subtract.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，是这个词内部的动词；同一词根还支撑着「抽出」「吸引」与「减去」。

items.en: Contrahere joined the prefix for 'together' with trahere, literally 'to draw together', and it came to mean making an agreement between parties.
items.cn: contrahere 把表示「共同」的前缀与 trahere 结合，字面为「拉到一起」，后来指在双方之间订立协议。

items.en: Contractus, the past participle used as a noun, meant a drawing together and hence a compact or agreement.
items.cn: contractus 是作名词用的过去分词，意为「拉在一起」，因而指一项协议或约款。

items.en: Law descends from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', related to the verb lay; it replaced an older English word for law.
items.cn: law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与动词「放置」相关；它取代了英语中较早表示法律的那个词。

items.en: English joined the borrowed noun for agreement to the northern word for law, and the compound named the rules about agreements.
items.cn: 英语把借来的「协议」名词与北方传入的「法律」一词结合，这个复合词指关于协议的规则。

items.en: The phrase became the name of a teaching subject and a branch of private law in the nineteenth century. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪成为一门教学科目与私法分支的名称。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for drawing and has split into a noun, an agent and a quite different physical sense; the second group places the subject among neighbouring branches of law.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「拉」的拉丁动词，并分成名词、施事者与一个相当不同的物理义；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的法律分支中。

entries.definition: The agreement itself, or the verb meaning to enter such an agreement, and separately to shrink; the entry phrase names only the law about it.
entries.definitionCN: 协议本身，或表示订立协议的动词，另有「收缩」一义；本短语只指关于它的法律。

entries.definition: A person or firm that takes on a contract to do work; the ending marks the agent rather than the legal subject.
entries.definitionCN: 承接合同工作的人或公司；词尾标示施事者，而不是法律部门。

entries.definition: The process of shrinking, or a shortened word form; it keeps the literal image of drawing together.
entries.definitionCN: 收缩的过程，或缩略的词形；它保留了「拉到一起」的字面形象。

entries.definition: To break a rule or law; it is built on a different Latin verb and has no link to drawing a bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则或法律；它建立在另一个拉丁动词上，与「拉成交易」无关。

entries.definition: The field covering duties that arise from agreements and from wrongdoing; the entry phrase is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖由协议与不法行为产生的义务的领域；本短语只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: The branch dealing with civil wrongs independent of any agreement; it sits beside the entry phrase rather than inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 处理与协议无关的民事侵害的部门；它与本短语并列，而不在其内。

entries.definition: The law of trade, firms and transactions; it uses contract rules but also covers companies, credit and sale of goods.
entries.definitionCN: 关于贸易、企业与交易的法律；它使用合同规则，但也涵盖公司、信贷与货物买卖。

entries.definition: A written law passed by a legislature; contract rules may come from statutes or from case law, so the two terms are not equivalents.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的成文法律；合同规则可能来自成文法或判例法，因此两者并不对等。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb for drawing together, the northern word for law, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「拉到一起」的动词、北方传入的「法律」一词、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core picture is two hands pulling a single knot tight.
normal.cn: 核心画面是两只手把同一个绳结拉紧。

normal.en: The family runs contract, contractual, contractually, contractor and contraction.
normal.cn: 同族词包括合同、合同的、依合同地、承包人与收缩。

normal.en: The subject follows a bargain through four stages: formation, consideration, interpretation and remedy.
normal.cn: 这门学科把一笔交易走过四步：成立、对价、解释与救济。

normal.en: Law did not come from Latin; it came from the north and meant something laid down.
normal.cn: 表示法律的这个词并非来自拉丁语；它来自北方，意为「被放下的东西」。

normal.en: A promise with nothing given in return is the classic example of a bond the law will not enforce.
normal.cn: 没有任何回报的承诺，是法律不予强制执行的绑缚的典型例子。

abstract.en: Picture two sheets of paper joined by a single thread, and a seal sitting exactly where the thread crosses.
abstract.cn: 想象两张纸被一根细线连起，印章正压在线交叉的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a knot that can be untied only by showing that one hand was forced.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结，只有证明其中一只手是被强迫的，才能解开。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of agreed words spanning two countries whose statutes never meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由商定文字搭成的桥，横跨两个法律从不相遇的国家。

examples.en: The case is studied in every introductory course on contract law.
examples.cn: 这个案例在每一门合同法入门课中都会被研读。

examples.en: Without consideration, the promise raises a question of contract law rather than of morality.
examples.cn: 没有对价时，这个承诺引出的是合同法问题，而不是道德问题。

examples.en: The two firms agreed to submit the dispute to a rule of contract law.
examples.cn: 两家公司同意把争议提交给某项合同规则处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捆得牢」——把双方捆在一起的约定，配上被定下的规矩，就是管着契约的那套法。

root: contract 出自拉丁语 contrahere「拉到一起」，由表示「共同」的前缀与 trahere「拉」构成，过去分词 contractus 指「协议」；law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与动词「放置」同源，属日耳曼语词。两者合成近代私法部门名称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings follow one bargain from knot to courtroom. The branch itself comes first; then the making of the bond through offer and acceptance and consideration; then how its words are read and what form it must take; then breach and remedy, the defences that untie it, and finally the international layer that lets bargains cross borders.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一笔交易从绳结走到法庭。先是这门学科本身；其次是通过要约、承诺与对价把绳结系成；再其次是文字如何被解读、需要何种形式；然后是违约与救济、解开绳结的抗辩，最后是让交易跨越国界的国际层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signed sheets joined at a seal, each side held by the same thread.
core.cn: 核心意象：两份签名的纸在印章处连成一体，双方被同一根线系住。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the body of rules that decides which promises the law will hold.
branches.cn: 学科本身：决定哪些承诺会被法律抓住的那套规则。

branches.en: FORMATION: the exchange of offer and acceptance, and the requirement that something be given on each side.
branches.cn: 成立：要约与承诺的交换，以及双方各须给出某物的要求。

branches.en: READING AND FORM: how the words are interpreted, and when paper, signature or seal is required.
branches.cn: 解读与形式：文字如何解释，以及何时需要纸面、签名或印章。

branches.en: REMEDY AND DEFENCE: what a broken promise costs, and the grounds that undo the bond entirely.
branches.cn: 救济与抗辩：违背承诺的代价，以及使绑缚整体失效的理由。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: conventions and standard terms for parties in different countries.
branches.cn: 跨境：为不同国家当事人准备的公约与标准条款。

intro.en: Two different histories meet: a Latin verb for drawing, which supplies the agreement half, and a Norse word for what is laid down, which supplies the law half.
intro.cn: 两段不同的历史在此相遇：一个表示「拉」的拉丁动词提供「协议」那一半，一个古诺尔斯语中表示「被放下之物」的词提供「法律」那一半。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below belong to the agreement half only; the law half is Germanic and has no Latin source in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式只属于「协议」那一半；「法律」那一半属日耳曼语，在这个家族中没有拉丁语来源。

items.meaningCN: 管束可执行协议的规则
items.example: The dispute was decided under contract law.
items.exampleCN: 该争议依合同法裁断。

items.meaning: an agreement drawn together by two parties
items.meaningCN: 由双方拉到一起的协议
items.example: The contract runs for three years.
items.exampleCN: 这份合同为期三年。

items.example: A contractual term cannot be ignored.
items.exampleCN: 合同条款不能被忽视。

items.example: The tenant is contractually bound to repair.
items.exampleCN: 租户依合同负有修缮义务。

items.meaning: one who takes on a contract
items.example: The contractor finished the bridge early.
items.exampleCN: 承包人提前完成了这座桥。

items.example: Cold causes a contraction of the metal.
items.exampleCN: 寒冷使金属收缩。

items.example: The press extracts oil from the seeds.
items.exampleCN: 压榨机从种子中榨油。

items.example: The magnet attracts iron filings.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁吸引铁屑。

items.meaning: to draw one number away from another
items.meaningCN: 把一个数从另一个数中减去
items.example: Subtract the costs from the revenue.
items.exampleCN: 从收入中减去成本。

latinEntries.meaning: to draw together; to make an agreement

derivatives.zh: 合同的；契约上的（名词加形容词后缀，指由合同约定或与合同有关的）
依合同地（形容词加副词后缀，指以合同条款为依据）
承包人；订约方（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指承接工程或服务的一方）
收缩；缩略（动词加表行为的名词后缀，语义由「拉到一起」转为「体积变小」或「词形缩短」）

definition_zh: 财产；所有物；房产；不动产；性质；特性
definition_en: something owned, especially land or buildings, or a quality that belongs to a thing
core_image: 一块地界石立在草地边缘，石面刻着主人的记号，旁边摆着屋内可搬动的器物
scene: 遗产清册上，房子、田地与家具都列在同一栏，标明归谁所有。The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
sceneCN: 这里指「归某人所有的财物与地产」，对应第 1 个义项：被拥有、可被继承的物；句意为清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏并注明归属。画面要点：地界石、主人的记号、并列的器物。

pos.zh: 财产；所有物；房产（不可数，指财物总体；表示一件件具体物品时可用复数）
性质；特性（可数，常用于科学语境，指某物固有的属性）

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

senses.title: Things that belong to someone
senses.definition: the things a person owns, taken as a whole, including goods, money and rights
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所拥有的东西的总和，包括货物、金钱与权利
senses.example: The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏，每件都注明属于某位继承人的财产。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'one's own', so the word begins as a label for whatever answers the question 'whose is it'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「自己的」，因此这个词起初就是给「这是谁的」这一问题的答案贴标签。

senses.title: Land and buildings
senses.definition: real estate, especially a house or plot that can be bought, sold or rented
senses.definitionCN: 不动产，尤指可买卖或出租的房屋或地块
senses.example: Property prices rose along the new railway.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路沿线的房价上涨了。
senses.why: Land is the one thing that cannot be carried away, so it became the clearest test of who owns what.
senses.whyCN: 土地是唯一搬不走的东西，因此它成为「谁拥有什么」最清楚的检验。

senses.title: The right of ownership itself
senses.definition: the legal power to use, exclude others from, sell or give away a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物、排除他人、出售或赠予该物的法律权力
senses.example: Property is a bundle of rights, not merely the object held.
senses.exampleCN: 所有权是一束权利，而不只是手中所持之物。
senses.why: Lawyers separate the object from the right over it, and the word covers both, which is why one can own property in property.
senses.whyCN: 法学家把物与对物的权利分开，而这个词同时覆盖两者，所以人可以对财产享有财产权。

senses.title: A quality belonging to a thing
senses.definition: a characteristic that a substance or object has, such as colour, hardness or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或物体所具有的特征，如颜色、硬度或导电性
senses.example: The property that makes the alloy useful is its resistance to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 使这种合金有用的性质是它的耐热性。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing in the oldest sense includes not only goods but traits, because a trait is also something 'its own'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老意义上的「属于」不只包括财物，也包括特征，因为特征同样是某物「自己的」东西。

senses.title: Property in intangible things
senses.definition: ownership of ideas, marks, designs or other intangibles protected by law
senses.definitionCN: 对思想、标记、设计或其他受法律保护的无形之物的所有权
senses.example: A song can be property even though nothing physical is held.
senses.exampleCN: 一首歌可以是财产，尽管手中并未握着任何实体。
senses.why: If ownership is a legal relation rather than a physical grip, it can attach to what cannot be touched.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有权是一种法律关系而不是一把握持，它就能附着在摸不到的东西上。

senses.title: Objects used on a stage
senses.definition: the movable articles that an actor handles in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或影片中操作的可移动物件
senses.example: The props master checks every property before the curtain rises.
senses.exampleCN: 道具管理员在幕启前检查每一件道具。
senses.why: The theatre borrowed the legal word for 'things owned by the company', shortened it, and kept the sense of objects that belong to a production.
senses.whyCN: 剧院借用了「剧团所有的物件」这一法律说法，把它缩短，保留了「属于某场演出之物」的意思。

senses.title: An attribute in logic and mathematics
senses.definition: a feature that may be predicated of an object, or a rule that a mathematical structure satisfies
senses.definitionCN: 可以述说某一对象的特征，或某一数学结构所满足的规则
senses.example: The proof uses a property shared by all prime numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明用到所有素数共有的一个属性。
senses.why: The quality sense, pushed to its most abstract, becomes whatever can be said to belong to a class of objects.
senses.whyCN: 「性质」义被推到最抽象处，就成为一切可以说属于某类对象的特征。

senses.title: An estate or domain in older use
senses.definition: a landed estate with its house and lands, especially in historical and literary descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 连同宅邸与土地在内的地产，尤见于历史与文学描写
senses.example: The old property passed to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧庄园传给了小儿子。
senses.why: Before land became a commodity it was an inherited domain, and that older meaning survives in descriptions of country estates.
senses.whyCN: 在土地成为商品之前，它是承袭而来的领地，这一较早的含义仍保留在对乡间地产的描写中。

intro.en: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership, quality', from proprius 'one's own'. The deeper origin of proprius is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been suggested but not settled. English took the word through Old French.
intro.cn: property 出自拉丁语 proprietas「所有权、性质」，源头为 proprius「自己的」。proprius 的更深来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但未成定论。英语经古法语吸收此词。

items.en: Proprius meant 'one's own, particular, not shared'; its own origin is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been proposed rather than proved.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的、不共享的」；它本身的来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但这只是提出而非证实。

items.en: Proprietas named both ownership and the quality that belongs to a thing, so the two later English senses were present from the start.
items.cn: proprietas 同时指所有权与某物固有的性质，因此后来英语中的两个义项从一开始就已存在。

items.en: Old French proprete carried both senses into English, where the legal and material side soon became dominant.
items.cn: 古法语 proprete 把两个义项都带入英语，其中法律与财物的一面很快占据主导。

items.en: In Middle English the word could still mean a quality, but land, goods and the right over them increasingly answered to it.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词仍可指性质，但土地、货物以及对它们的权利越来越多地用它来表达。

items.en: In modern usage the material sense dominates law and everyday speech, while the quality sense survives mainly in science and logic. The date of this separation is approximate.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，财物义主导法律与日常表达，而性质义主要保存在科学与逻辑中。这一分家的年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective for 'one's own' but has drifted into fitness, decorum and exclusivity; the second group gives near alternatives for belongings and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个表示「自己的」拉丁形容词构成，但已漂向合适、得体与独占；第二组是「财物」与「性质」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: Correct or suitable, and in some phrases meaning 'itself'; the sense moved from 'belonging to a thing' to 'fitting that thing'.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，在某些短语中意为「本身」；语义由「属于某物」转为「合乎某物」。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour or of usage; it comes from the same source but describes what is fitting rather than what is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或用语得体；它出自同一来源，但描述合乎礼仪之事，而不是被拥有之物。

entries.definition: Owned by a particular person or firm, or sold under an exclusive name; it is the adjective built on the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定个人或公司所有的，或以独占名称销售的；它是建立在所有权义上的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural means several pieces of real estate or several qualities; the theatre shortening props belongs here too.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式可指数处房产或数种性质；剧院用语中的缩略形式也归在这里。

entries.definition: The fact of having something in one's control; it can exist without legal ownership, which is why the two are distinguished in law.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于某人控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律上的所有权而存在，因此法律上把两者区分开。

entries.definition: Anything of value owned, seen from the balance sheet; it is a financial category rather than a legal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的任何有价值之物，从资产负债表的角度看；它是一个财务类别，而不是法律关系。

entries.definition: A large area of land with a house, or the total property a person leaves at death; it is narrower than the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 带有宅邸的大片土地，或某人去世时留下的全部财产；它比本词窄。

entries.definition: A characteristic regarded as belonging to a person or thing; it covers the quality sense of the entry word but never the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为属于某人或某物的特征；它覆盖本词的性质义，却从不覆盖所有权义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for 'one's own', real derived words and real legal phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词、真实派生词与真实法律用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Everything starts from the question 'whose is it', which is what 'one's own' answers.
normal.cn: 一切都从「这是谁的」这个问题开始，而「自己的」正是它的答案。

normal.en: The family runs proper, propriety, proprietor, proprietary and proprietorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括恰当的、得体、所有人、专有的与所有权。

normal.en: The same word covers the object and the right over it, so lawyers speak of property in property.
normal.cn: 同一个词既覆盖物，也覆盖对物的权利，因此法学家会说对财产享有财产权。

normal.en: Land is the clearest property because it cannot be carried away.
normal.cn: 土地是最清楚的财产，因为它搬不走。

normal.en: The theatre shortened the word to props, and the stage sense is still alive.
normal.cn: 剧院把这个词缩短为「道具」，舞台义至今仍活在使用中。

abstract.en: Picture a stone at the edge of a field with a name cut into it, and a chair, a cup and a coat laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野边缘一块刻着名字的石头，旁边摆着一把椅子、一只杯子和一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent box around an idea, marked with the same seal as the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明的盒子罩住一个想法，盒上盖着与房屋相同的印章。

abstract.en: Picture a substance whose label reads not 'mine' but 'this is what I am like'.
abstract.cn: 想象一种物质的标签上写的不是「我的」，而是「我本来就是这样」。

examples.en: The firm owns property in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市拥有房产。

examples.en: Hardness is a property that the alloy keeps at high temperature.
examples.cn: 硬度是这种合金在高温下仍保持的一种性质。

examples.en: The lease set out who was responsible for repairs to the property.
examples.cn: 租约列明了谁负责该房产的修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破坡地」——坡上那块地也是家产；再记住同一词还能指物之本性，就像地有坡、铁有硬。

root: 拉丁语 proprius「自己的、特有的」→ proprietas「所有权、性质」→ 经古法语 proprete 进入英语。proprius 的更深来源不确定，出自「为个体所有」短语的说法属假说；同根词包括 proper、propriety、proprietor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from what answers 'whose is it'. The owned things come first, with land and buildings as the clearest case; then the right of ownership itself, which can attach even to untouchable things; then the quality that belongs to a thing, at home in science and logic; and finally the stage objects and the older landed estate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「这是谁的」这一答案长出。先是被拥有的东西，其中土地与房屋最清楚；其次是对物享有所有权的权利，它甚至可以附着在摸不到的东西上；再其次是某物固有的性质，在科学与逻辑中安家；最后是舞台道具与较早的地产庄园义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone with a name on it, and the things inside the line that answer to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着名字的地界石，以及界线之内属于这个名字的一切。

branches.en: THINGS: belongings in general, and the objects a theatre company owns for a production.
branches.cn: 物：一般意义上的财物，以及剧团为某场演出所拥有的物件。

branches.en: LAND: the immovable core, houses and plots that cannot be carried off.
branches.cn: 土地：不可移动的内核，搬不走的房屋与地块。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: ownership as a legal power, extending to intangibles such as songs and marks.
branches.cn: 权利：作为法律权力的所有权，可延伸到歌曲与标记等无形之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: what belongs to a thing's nature, in the laboratory and in logic.
branches.cn: 性质：属于某物本性的东西，在实验室里也在逻辑中。

branches.en: ESTATE: the older landed domain, inherited rather than traded.
branches.cn: 庄园：较早的领地，承袭而来而非买卖所得。

intro.en: One Latin adjective for 'one's own' supplies the whole family, with noun and agent endings added; the sense splits between what is owned and what a thing is like.
intro.cn: 一个表示「自己的」的拉丁形容词提供了整个家族，随后加上名词与施事后缀；语义在「被拥有之物」与「某物像什么」之间分开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及作名词用的中性形式。

items.example: The property passed to the eldest child.
items.exampleCN: 这份财产传给了长子。

items.example: The two properties share a fence.
items.exampleCN: 这两处房产共用一道篱笆。

items.example: That is the proper way to fold the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 那才是折这块布的正确方法。

items.example: The machine must be properly sealed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器必须妥善密封。

items.example: The guests observed the proprieties of the house.
items.exampleCN: 客人们遵守这户人家的礼节。

items.meaning: the owner of a business or estate
items.example: The proprietor greeted us at the door.
items.exampleCN: 业主在门口迎接我们。

items.example: The software is proprietary and cannot be copied.
items.exampleCN: 该软件为专有软件，不得复制。

items.example: The business is under sole proprietorship.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业属独资所有。

items.meaning: to take as one's own; suitable
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 议会拨出款项用于这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: a thing of one's own; a characteristic

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

definition_en: the state or legal right of possessing something, or the relation by which a thing belongs to a person
core_image: 一枚刻着名字的铜牌钉在门上，钥匙挂在旁边，名字在牌上的人就有权处置屋内之物
scene: 产权登记处把房屋过户到买方名下，登记簿上的名字一换，处置权随之转移。The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
sceneCN: 这里指「对某物享有法律上的所有权」，对应第 1 个义项：可以占有、使用与处置的权利；句意为登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。画面要点：门上的铜牌、挂着的钥匙、登记簿。

pos.zh: 所有权；拥有（不可数，常后接表示所属物的介词短语，指明所拥有之物）

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

senses.title: The legal right to dispose of a thing
senses.titleCN: 对物进行处置的法律权利
senses.definition: the legal power to use, sell, give away or exclude others from a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用、出售、赠予某物并排除他人使用的法律权力
senses.example: The land registry transferred the house to the buyer, and once the name on the register changed, ownership passed with it.
senses.exampleCN: 产权登记处把房屋过户给买方，登记簿上的名字一换，所有权随之转移。
senses.why: The word joins the verb 'to have' to a suffix for a condition, so it names a state of having that the law will protect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表示「拥有」的动词与表状态的后缀结合，命名一种法律会保护的有有状态。

senses.title: Holding something in fact
senses.definition: the actual possession of a thing, whether or not the law recognises a title
senses.definitionCN: 实际持有某物，无论法律是否承认其权属
senses.example: Ownership of the keys does not always mean ownership of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 拿着钥匙并不总意味着拥有这套公寓。
senses.why: Possession and title can come apart, and the word sometimes describes the plain fact of having rather than the right to have.
senses.whyCN: 占有与权属可以分开，这个词有时描述「手上确实有」这一事实，而不是「有权拥有」。

senses.title: The relation of belonging
senses.definition: the link by which a thing is attributed to a person, so that it answers to that person's name
senses.definitionCN: 某物被归到某人名下、对其名字作出回应的那种联系
senses.example: Ownership of the manuscript is disputed between two libraries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿的归属在两家图书馆之间存有争议。
senses.why: Beyond the right and the fact lies a relation: the thing belongs to someone, and that belonging is what the noun most abstractly names.
senses.whyCN: 在权利与事实之外还有一层关系：物属于某人，而这种归属正是这个名词最抽象地命名的东西。

senses.title: Shareholding and proprietorship
senses.definition: the holding of shares in a company, or the position of a person who owns a firm
senses.definitionCN: 持有公司股份，或拥有某企业的业主地位
senses.example: Foreign ownership of the airline was capped at a fixed share.
senses.exampleCN: 该航空公司的外资持股被限定在固定比例内。
senses.why: When firms replace land as the main object of wealth, the same noun measures who holds the shares.
senses.whyCN: 当企业取代土地成为财富的主要对象，同一个名词就用来衡量谁持有股份。

senses.title: Public versus private regimes
senses.titleCN: 公有与私有的制度之分
senses.definition: the system under which the means of production or a service is held by the state or by private persons
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料或某项服务由国家持有还是由私人持有的制度安排
senses.example: The dispute was about ownership of the water supply, not about its price.
senses.exampleCN: 争论在于供水归谁所有，而不在于水价。
senses.why: Ownership becomes a political question once whole industries rather than single objects are at stake.
senses.whyCN: 一旦涉及的是整个行业而不是单件物品，所有权就成了政治问题。

senses.title: Personal responsibility for a task
senses.definition: the attitude of treating a problem or project as one's own, with the duty to see it through
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题或项目当作自己的事、并承担完成责任的态度
senses.example: The team asked each member to take ownership of one part of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 团队要求每位成员对计划的一部分负起责任。
senses.why: Modern management borrowed the legal word and stripped the title from it, leaving only the sense of treating the work as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理借用了这个法律词，抽去了权属，只留下「把工作当作自己的事」这一层。

senses.title: Attribution of a work to its author
senses.definition: the legal and moral link between a creative work and the person who made it
senses.definitionCN: 创造性作品与其创作者之间的法律与道义联系
senses.example: Ownership of the copyright passed to the publisher for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权中的财产权在十年内转给了出版方。
senses.why: A text or a design can belong to someone too, so the noun extends from goods to works of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 文本或设计同样可以属于某人，因此这个名词从货物延伸到心智作品。

senses.title: Tenure of land in older law
senses.definition: the holding of land under a lord or a superior, with duties attached, rather than outright title
senses.definitionCN: 在领主或上级之下持有土地并附带义务，而不是绝对的所有权
senses.example: In that period ownership of land carried service as well as rent.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个时期，土地保有权既带来地租，也带来服役义务。
senses.why: Before absolute title was common, holding land meant holding it of someone, and the word recorded that layered relation.
senses.whyCN: 在绝对所有权普及之前，持有土地意味着从某人那里持有，这个词记录了那种分层的关系。

intro.en: Ownership joins the Old English verb agan 'to have, possess' to the suffix -ship, which came from a word for shape or condition. Both parts are Germanic, and the compound is a native English formation rather than a borrowing.
intro.cn: ownership 由古英语动词 agan「拥有、占有」加后缀 -ship 构成，而后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词。两部分都属日耳曼语，这个复合词是英语本族造词，而不是借词。

items.en: Agan 'to have, to possess' is the verb behind own, and it is Germanic, with recorded relatives in other old Germanic languages.
items.cn: agan 意为「有、占有」，是 own 背后的动词，属日耳曼语，在其他古老日耳曼语言中有可考的同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed verb is posited with a star; the deeper Indo-European root is also a reconstruction, so the earliest layer is not directly attested.
items.cn: 重构的动词形式以带星号的方式拟出；更深的印欧语词根同样属重构，因此最早的层次没有直接文献实证。

items.en: The suffix came from a word meaning 'shape, condition', and it built nouns for states, offices and skills.
items.cn: 这个后缀出自一个表示「形状、状态」的词，用来构成表示状态、职位与技艺的名词。

items.en: The compound joined the two and named the condition of one who has something, at first in ordinary rather than legal language.
items.cn: 这个复合词把两者结合，命名「拥有某物者的状态」，最初用于日常语言而非法律语言。

items.en: Lawyers later separated ownership from mere holding, giving the noun a technical sense that possession alone does not fill.
items.cn: 法学家后来把所有权与单纯的占有分开，使这个名词获得一个单靠占有无法填补的专业含义。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word also came to mean personal responsibility for a task. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词也开始指对任务负起个人责任。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built from the same verb or looks close to it; the second group gives near alternatives from law, accounting and plain possession.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个动词构成或与它形近；第二组是来自法律、会计与日常占有三个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: To possess, or belonging to oneself, as in one's own; it is the source word, while the entry noun names the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有，或属于自己，如「自己的」；它是来源词，而本名词命名那种关系。

entries.definition: The person who holds title to a thing; the suffix marks a person, so the word cannot name the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物持有权属的人；后缀标示人，因此这个词不能命名关系本身。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in an owing sum; it comes from the verb owe, which is a different word from own.
entries.definitionCN: 尚待支付的，如「欠款」；它出自动词「欠」，与「拥有」是不同的词。

entries.definition: A person who owns the home he lives in; it joins the owner word to a word for occupying.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有并居住在自己房屋的人；它把「所有者」与「占用」两个词连在一起。

entries.definition: The fact of having something under one's control; it can exist without legal title, which is why the two are distinguished.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律权属而存在，因此两者被区分开。

entries.definition: The status of an owner, especially of a business; it is close in meaning but more formal and more often used of firms.
entries.definitionCN: 所有人的身份，尤指企业所有人；它意思相近，但更正式，也更常用于企业。

entries.definition: The legal right to own property, or the document proving it; it is the lawyer's word for the proof rather than the relation.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有财产的合法权利，或证明它的文件；它是法学家用来指证明而非关系的词。

entries.definition: The care and control of a person or thing, often without ownership; a custodian may hold what belongs to another.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或在物的照管与控制，往往不含所有权；保管人可以持有属于他人之物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English verb for having, the native suffix for a condition, real derived words and real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语中表示「有」的动词、本族语中表状态的后缀、真实派生词与真实法律用语。

normal.en: The core is a name on a door: the thing answers to that name.
normal.cn: 核心是门上刻着的一个名字：那件东西对那个名字作出回应。

normal.en: The family runs own, owner, owners and co-ownership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括拥有、所有者、各位所有者与共有。

normal.en: Law separates the right from the holding, which is why possession alone is not ownership.
normal.cn: 法律把权利与占有分开，所以单有占有并不构成所有权。

normal.en: A company can be owned as surely as a field, so the word measures shares as well as soil.
normal.cn: 公司可以像田地一样被拥有，因此这个词既衡量股份，也衡量土地。

normal.en: Modern managers ask staff to take ownership of a problem, which keeps only the sense of treating it as one's own.
normal.cn: 现代管理者要求员工对问题「负起责任」，这里只保留了「把它当作自己的事」这一层。

abstract.en: Picture a brass plate on a door with a name cut into it, and a key hanging from the same hook.
abstract.cn: 想象门上钉着一块刻了名字的铜牌，同一只钩子上挂着钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a register whose page is rewritten, and the right to the house moving with the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一本登记簿的页面被改写，房屋的权利随墨迹一起转移。

abstract.en: Picture a worker who writes his own name on a task that no one assigned to him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名工人把名字写在一件没有人指派给他的任务上。

examples.en: Ownership of the building was split between two families.
examples.cn: 这栋楼的所有权由两户人家分有。

examples.en: The report recommends wider home ownership among younger households.
examples.cn: 报告建议让更多年轻家庭拥有自有住房。

examples.en: She took ownership of the delay and explained what went wrong.
examples.cn: 她承担了延误的责任，并解释了出错之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧呢事普」——「欧」听成「我」，「呢」听成「的」：写着我的名字的那件东西，就是所有权。

root: 古英语 agan「拥有、占有」+ 古英语 -scipe「形状、状态」→ ownership。两部分均属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语来源；该动词的日耳曼语祖形与更深的印欧语词根都属重构形式，无直接文献实证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a name on a door. The legal right to dispose comes first, then the plain fact of holding, then belonging as a relation; from there the word measures shares, divides public from private regimes, lends itself to personal responsibility, extends to works of the mind, and remembers an older layered tenure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从门上刻着的名字开始。先是对物处置的法律权利，其次是持有的事实，再其次是归属这一关系；由此这个词衡量股份、区分公有与私有、借给个人责任感、延伸到心智作品，并记得一种较早的分层保有权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name on a plate beside a key, marking who may dispose of what is behind the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙旁铜牌上的名字，标明谁有权处置门后之物。

branches.en: RIGHT AND HOLDING: the legal power to dispose, and the bare fact of having something in hand.
branches.cn: 权利与持有：处置的法律权力，以及手中确实有某物的事实。

branches.en: BELONGING: the relation that ties a thing to a name, including the older layered tenure of land.
branches.cn: 归属：把物与名字系在一起的关系，包括较早的分层土地保有权。

branches.en: SHARES: ownership measured in stock, and the position of a firm's proprietor.
branches.cn: 股份：以股票衡量的所有权，以及企业业主的地位。

branches.en: REGIMES: the political division between public and private holding.
branches.cn: 制度：公有与私有之间的政治分野。

branches.en: RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORSHIP: treating a task as one's own, and attributing a work to its maker.
branches.cn: 责任与作者身份：把任务当作自己的事，以及把作品归到创作者名下。

intro.en: This family is entirely Germanic: a verb for having plus a native suffix for a condition, with compounds built by adding person and place words.
intro.cn: 这个家族完全是日耳曼语的：一个表示「拥有」的动词，加上一个本族语的表状态后缀，再由表示人与处所的词构成复合形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this family. Latin-based near synonyms such as possession and proprietorship come from different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个家族没有拉丁语来源。由拉丁语派生的近义词如「占有」与「所有权」出自不同的词根。

items.meaning: the condition of holding something as one's own
items.meaningCN: 把某物作为自己之物持有的状态
items.example: Ownership passed to the buyer on signature.
items.exampleCN: 签署之时所有权转移给买方。

items.example: They own the land beside the river.
items.exampleCN: 他们拥有河边那块地。

items.example: The owner refused to sell.
items.exampleCN: 业主拒绝出售。

items.example: The owners met to divide the rent.
items.exampleCN: 各位业主开会分配租金。

items.meaning: a holder of title shared with another
items.example: Each co-owner may use the whole garden.
items.exampleCN: 每位共有人都可以使用整个花园。

items.meaning: title shared by more than one person
items.example: Co-ownership requires agreement on repairs.
items.exampleCN: 共有要求就修缮达成一致。

items.example: The landowner leased the field for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 地主把这块田租了十年。

items.meaning: a person who owns the house he lives in
items.example: Homeowners pay a local property tax.
items.exampleCN: 房主需缴纳地方房产税。

items.example: Their friendship began at school.
items.exampleCN: 他们的友谊始于学校。

derivatives.zh: 所有者；物主（动词加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
共有人（表示「共同」的前缀与所有者一词复合，指与他人共享所有权的人）
共有；共同所有（表示「共同」的前缀与所有权一词复合，指所有权由多人分享）
拥有；承认（古英语动词，指对某物有支配权，后引申为「承认某事属于自己」）

definition_en: the legal rights over creations of the mind, such as inventions, texts, designs, marks and secrets
core_image: 一只灯泡里长出一本书与一段旋律，外面罩着一层写着「归创作者」的玻璃罩
scene: 律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件，统一称为知识产权。The firm grouped patents, trademarks and copyright under one heading and called them intellectual property.
sceneCN: 这里指「对智力创造成果享有的一组法律权利」，对应第 1 个义项：把发明、文本、标记等无形成果当作财产来保护；句意为律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件。画面要点：灯泡、书与旋律、玻璃罩。

pos.zh: 知识产权（不可数，作集合名称；指各类具体权利时可作可数用）

derivatives.zh: 智力的；知识分子的（拉丁语中表示「理解」的动词加形容词后缀，指与思考能力有关的）
在智力上（形容词加副词后缀，指从思考能力的角度）
智力；才智（由拉丁语中表示「在…之间挑选」的动词加名词词尾构成，指理解与判断的能力）
智力；情报（同源动词加表性质的名词后缀，语义由「理解」扩展到「理解的结果」与「情报」）

senses.title: Rights over creations of the mind
senses.titleCN: 对智力创造成果的权利总称
senses.definition: the whole family of legal rights that treat inventions, texts, designs and marks as property
senses.definitionCN: 把发明、文本、设计与标记当作财产来保护的一整族法律权利
senses.example: The firm grouped patents, trademarks and copyright under one heading and called them intellectual property.
senses.exampleCN: 律所把专利、商标与著作权归入同一类案件，统称知识产权。
senses.why: The phrase takes the adjective for thinking and joins it to the noun for what is owned, so a product of the mind is treated as a thing that can belong to someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表示思考的形容词与表示被拥有之物的名词连在一起，于是心智的产物被当作可以归属某人的东西。

senses.title: Patents over inventions
senses.definition: the exclusive right, granted for a limited term, to make or sell a new invention
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内被授予的、制造或销售某项新发明的独占权利
senses.example: A patent is the intellectual property that protects a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 专利是保护一台机器的知识产权。
senses.why: An invention is useful only if it can be worked, so the right is framed as an exclusive power to work it for a set number of years.
senses.whyCN: 发明只有能被实施才有用，因此这项权利被构造成在固定年数内独家实施它的权力。

senses.title: Copyright over texts and music
senses.titleCN: 文本与音乐上的著作权
senses.definition: the right to control copying, performance and adaptation of a written or recorded work
senses.definitionCN: 控制文字或录音作品的复制、表演与改编的权利
senses.example: Copyright protects the melody but not the idea of a song about winter.
senses.exampleCN: 著作权保护那段旋律，却不保护「写一首关于冬天的歌」这个想法。
senses.why: A text can be copied without being taken away, so the right is aimed at copying rather than at possession.
senses.whyCN: 文本可以被复制而并未被夺走，因此这项权利针对的是复制，而不是占有。

senses.title: Trademarks over signs of origin
senses.definition: the right to prevent others from using a sign that identifies the source of goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 阻止他人使用标示商品或服务来源的标记的权利
senses.example: The logo is intellectual property that tells buyers who made the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标识是知识产权，它告诉买方商品由谁制造。
senses.why: A mark has value only because customers rely on it, so the right protects the buyer's recognition as much as the owner's name.
senses.whyCN: 标记之所以有价值，只因为顾客依赖它，因此这项权利既保护所有者的名号，也保护买方的辨识。

senses.title: Trade secrets
senses.definition: protection of confidential information that gives a business an advantage, without publishing it
senses.definitionCN: 对使企业取得优势的保密信息予以保护，而不将其公开
senses.example: The formula is protected as a trade secret rather than as intellectual property registered in an office.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方作为商业秘密受到保护，而不是作为在主管部门登记的知识产权。
senses.why: Some creations lose their value the moment they are published, so the law protects secrecy instead of granting a public monopoly.
senses.whyCN: 有些创造成果一旦公开就失去价值，因此法律保护的是保密，而不是授予公开的垄断。

senses.title: Industrial designs
senses.definition: the right over the outward appearance of a product, such as its shape, pattern or ornament
senses.definitionCN: 对产品外观（如形状、图案或装饰）享有的权利
senses.example: The shape of the bottle is protected as an industrial design.
senses.exampleCN: 这个瓶子的形状作为外观设计受到保护。
senses.why: Between an invention and a work of art lies a product's look, and the law created a right to cover exactly that middle ground.
senses.whyCN: 在发明与艺术品之间隔着产品的外观，法律创制了一项恰好覆盖这段中间地带的权。

senses.title: The international system
senses.definition: the treaties and offices that let a right obtained in one country be recognised in others
senses.definitionCN: 使在一国取得的权利在别国也获承认的条约与机构
senses.example: A single application can now reach many offices through the international system for intellectual property.
senses.exampleCN: 通过知识产权的国际体系，一份申请现在可以送抵许多主管机构。
senses.why: Ideas cross borders more easily than goods, so the rights over them needed a layer of treaties and common offices.
senses.whyCN: 思想比货物更容易跨越国界，因此对思想的权利需要一层条约与共同的机构。

senses.title: New objects in the digital age
senses.definition: the extension of the same rights to databases, software and algorithms
senses.definitionCN: 把同一组权利扩展到数据库、软件与算法
senses.example: The dispute over the database is a dispute about intellectual property in a new form.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个数据库的争议，是关于新形态知识产权的争议。
senses.why: Every new medium produces something that can be copied cheaply, and the old family of rights is stretched to cover it.
senses.whyCN: 每一种新媒介都会产生可被廉价复制的东西，于是旧的权利家族被拉长去覆盖它。

intro.en: Intellectual descends from Latin intelligere 'to understand', built on legere 'to choose, gather, read'. Property comes from proprietas 'ownership'. The English phrase was formed in the nineteenth century, when patents and copyright began to be classed together as property.
intro.cn: intellectual 出自拉丁语 intelligere「理解」，建立在 legere「挑选、收集、读」之上。property 出自 proprietas「所有权」。这个英语短语在十九世纪形成，当时专利与著作权开始被归为一类财产。

items.en: Legere meant 'to choose, gather, read'; its sense of picking out explains both reading and the later idea of understanding.
items.cn: legere 意为「挑选、收集、读」；其中「挑出」的意思既解释了阅读，也解释了后来「理解」的观念。

items.en: Intelligere joined the prefix for 'between, among' with legere, literally 'to choose among', and came to mean understanding.
items.cn: intelligere 把表示「在…之间」的前缀与 legere 结合，字面为「在其中挑选」，后来意为理解。

items.en: The adjective intellectualis described what belongs to the understanding rather than to the senses.
items.cn: 形容词 intellectualis 描述属于理解力而非感官的事物。

items.en: Proprietas named ownership, and English property inherited both the legal sense and the sense of a quality.
items.cn: proprietas 指所有权，英语中的 property 继承了它的法律义与「性质」义。

items.en: The phrase was formed in the nineteenth century, when patents, copyright and marks began to be treated as one kind of property. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪形成，当时专利、著作权与商标开始被当作同一类财产。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for choosing and reading but has split into understanding, clarity and a social type; the second group gives the neighbouring legal categories.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「挑选与阅读」的拉丁动词，但已分成理解、清晰与一种社会身份；第二组是相邻的法律类别。

entries.definition: The power of understanding and reasoning; it names the capacity, not the rights over what the capacity produces.
entries.definitionCN: 理解与推理的能力；它命名能力本身，而不是对能力产物所享的权利。

entries.definition: Able to learn and reason well; it describes a person or device rather than a legal category.
entries.definitionCN: 善于学习与推理的；它描述人或设备，而不是一个法律类别。

entries.definition: Capable of being understood; it concerns how clear something is, not who owns it.
entries.definitionCN: 可被理解的；它关心某物有多清楚，而不是归谁所有。

entries.definition: The view that reason is the chief source of knowledge; it is a philosophical position, not a property right.
entries.definitionCN: 认为理性是知识主要来源的主张；它是一种哲学立场，不是财产权。

entries.definition: A non-physical item of value on a balance sheet; it is wider and includes goodwill and brands that may not be protected rights.
entries.definitionCN: 资产负债表中不具实体的有价值项目；它范围更宽，包括未必受权利保护的商誉与品牌。

entries.definition: The older name for patents, marks and designs, as opposed to literary and artistic works.
entries.definitionCN: 专利、商标与外观设计较早的称法，与文学艺术作品相对。

entries.definition: The specific right over copying and performance of a work; it is one part of the entry phrase, not its whole.
entries.definitionCN: 对作品复制与表演的具体权利；它是本短语的一部分，而不是全部。

entries.definition: An exclusive right granted for an invention; like copyright it is one branch of the wider family.
entries.definitionCN: 为一项发明授予的独占权利；与著作权一样，它只是更大家族中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verbs for choosing and understanding, the noun for ownership, real derived words and real legal categories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「挑选」与「理解」的动词、表示所有权的名词、真实派生词与真实法律类别。

normal.en: The first word points to the mind, the second to ownership, so the phrase means owning what the mind makes.
normal.cn: 前一个词指向心智，后一个词指向所有，因此这个短语意为拥有心智所造之物。

normal.en: The family runs intellect, intellectual, intellectually and intelligence.
normal.cn: 同族词包括智力、智力的、在智力上，以及由同一词根发展出的「情报」一词。

normal.en: The field has four common members: patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret.
normal.cn: 这个领域有四个常见成员：专利、著作权、商标与商业秘密。

normal.en: A song can be protected even though nothing physical is held, which is why the phrase speaks of property in an idea.
normal.cn: 一首歌可以在没有任何实体持有时受到保护，所以这个短语说的是对想法的财产。

normal.en: Registration offices and treaties exist because ideas cross borders more easily than goods.
normal.cn: 登记机构与条约之所以存在，是因为思想比货物更容易跨越国界。

abstract.en: Picture a glass dome over a light bulb, a book and a scrap of melody, with a name written on the dome.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃罩罩住灯泡、书与一小段旋律，罩上写着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens only the copy of a text and never the original.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙只能打开文本的复制件，却永远打不开原件。

abstract.en: Picture a locked drawer inside a factory that holds a formula no one is allowed to see.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂里一只上锁的抽屉，里面放着不许任何人查看的配方。

examples.en: The treaty raised the level of protection for intellectual property.
examples.cn: 该条约提高了知识产权的保护水平。

examples.en: Small firms often fail to register their intellectual property in time.
examples.cn: 小企业常常未能及时登记自己的知识产权。

examples.en: The case turned on whether a database counts as intellectual property.
examples.cn: 该案的争点在于数据库是否算作知识产权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑袋里的家产」——先想「智力」，再想「财产」：凡是脑子造出来、又能被复制的，都可以像房产一样登记归属。

root: intellectual 出自拉丁语 intelligere「理解」，由表示「在…之间」的前缀与 legere「挑选、读」构成；property 出自 proprietas「所有权」，源头为 proprius「自己的」，其更深来源不确定。整个短语是十九世纪形成的法律复合名称。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings fan out from one idea: the mind's product treated as property. The general family comes first; then patents, copyright, marks, secrets and designs, each protecting a different kind of creation; then the international layer that carries the rights across borders; and finally the new objects of the digital age.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个观念展开：把心智的产物当作财产。先是整个家族；其次是专利、著作权、商标、商业秘密与外观设计，各自保护不同种类的创造；再其次是让权利跨越国界的国际层面；最后是数字时代的新对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a creation of the mind enclosed in a dome bearing the maker's name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件心智创造被罩在写有创作者名字的玻璃罩里。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the general name for rights over creations of the mind.
branches.cn: 家族：对智力创造成果所享权利的总称。

branches.en: INVENTION AND DESIGN: a working machine, and the outward look of a product.
branches.cn: 发明与设计：一台能运转的机器，以及一个产品的外表。

branches.en: TEXT AND MELODY: the right aimed at copying rather than at possession.
branches.cn: 文本与旋律：针对复制而非占有的权利。

branches.en: MARKS AND SECRETS: signs that identify a source, and information kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 标记与秘密：标示来源的符号，以及被藏在视线之外的信息。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND NEW FORMS: treaties that cross borders, and databases and software that stretch the old family.
branches.cn: 保护与新形态：跨越国界的条约，以及拉长旧家族边界的数据库与软件。

intro.en: Two Latin strands meet: a verb for choosing and reading, which gives the whole intellect family, and an adjective for 'one's own', which gives property and its relatives.
intro.cn: 两条拉丁语线索在此相遇：一个表示「挑选与阅读」的动词给出整个智力词族，一个表示「自己的」形容词给出「财产」及其亲属词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the verb of understanding, its noun and adjective, and the noun for ownership.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了表示理解的动词、它的名词与形容词，以及表示所有权的名词。

items.meaning: rights over creations of the mind
items.meaningCN: 对智力创造成果的权利
items.example: The licence covers the intellectual property in the design.
items.exampleCN: 该许可涵盖设计中的知识产权。

items.example: The work demands an intellectual effort.
items.exampleCN: 这项工作需要智力上的努力。

items.example: The puzzle is intellectually satisfying.
items.exampleCN: 这个谜题在智力上令人满足。

items.example: Her intellect was never in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 她的才智从未受到怀疑。

items.meaning: the ability to learn; information gathered
items.meaningCN: 学习能力；收集到的情报
items.example: The test measures intelligence rather than memory.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试衡量的是智力而不是记忆。

items.example: The manual is intelligible to a beginner.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册对初学者也读得懂。

items.meaning: the view that reason leads to knowledge
items.meaningCN: 认为理性通向知识的主张
items.example: The essay criticises narrow intellectualism.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章批评狭隘的唯理主义。

items.example: The design is the company's property.
items.exampleCN: 这项设计是公司的财产。

items.example: The formula remains proprietary.
items.exampleCN: 该配方仍属专有。

derivatives.zh: 智力的；知识分子的（拉丁语中表示「理解」的动词加形容词后缀，指与思考能力有关的）
在智力上（形容词加副词后缀，指从思考能力的角度）
智力；才智（由拉丁语中表示「在…之间挑选」的动词加名词词尾构成，指理解与判断的能力）
智力；情报（同源动词加表性质的名词后缀，语义由「理解」扩展到「理解的结果」与「情报」）

definition_zh: 物理学；物理；（口语）事物的物理特性与运作原理
definition_en: the science of matter, energy, motion and the forces that govern them, or the physical way something works
core_image: 一只摆锤从最高点落下，旁边并排放着温度计、磁铁与棱镜，都在量同一件事：物体如何运动与相互作用
scene: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，试图用同一条定律解释两种现象。In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究物质、运动与相互作用的物理学」，对应第 1 个义项：作为一门学科的整体；句意为学生用同一条物理定律解释单摆与透镜两种现象。画面要点：摆锤、温度计、磁铁、棱镜。

pos.zh: 物理学（不可数，作学科名称；口语中也可指某物的运作机制）

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）
形而上学（表示「之后、超越」的前缀与物理学复合，原指编在物理学之后的讨论，后指研究存在本身的学问）

senses.title: The science of matter and motion
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与运动的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, forces and the structure of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量、运动、力以及宇宙结构的那门科学
senses.example: In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，希望同一条物理定律能解释两者。
senses.why: The Greek source named 'natural things', so the discipline begins as the study of whatever happens by nature rather than by human arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「自然之物」，因此这门学科起初研究的是依本性而非依人造安排发生的一切。

senses.title: How a particular thing works
senses.titleCN: 某具体事物的运作原理
senses.definition: the physical principles behind a device, a sport or a natural event
senses.definitionCN: 某个装置、某项运动或某种自然现象背后的物理原理
senses.example: The coach explained the physics of a spinning ball.
senses.exampleCN: 教练讲解了旋转球的物理原理。
senses.why: The name of a whole discipline can be applied to one small case, because every case is an instance of the same laws.
senses.whyCN: 整门学科的名称可以用在一个小案例上，因为每个案例都是同一批定律的实例。

senses.title: Classical mechanics in practice
senses.definition: the part of the subject dealing with bodies moving well below the speed of light, as formulated before relativity
senses.definitionCN: 研究远低于光速运动的物体、在相对论之前已成体系的那部分内容
senses.example: The bridge design was checked with classical physics.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁设计用经典物理作了校核。
senses.why: The old core of the subject kept the plain name, so 'physics' often means the mechanics of ordinary speeds and sizes.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科旧有的核心保留了这个朴素的名字，因此「物理」常指日常速度与尺度下的力学。

senses.title: Relativity and the quantum
senses.titleCN: 相对论与量子层面的现代物理
senses.definition: the parts of the subject that describe very fast, very massive or very small systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述极快、极重或极小系统的那部分内容
senses.example: Modern physics begins where the classical laws stop working.
senses.exampleCN: 现代物理从经典定律失效之处开始。
senses.why: When the old laws failed at the extremes, the same word had to cover the theories that replaced them.
senses.whyCN: 当旧定律在极端情形下失效，同一个词就必须覆盖取而代之的新理论。

senses.title: Branch subjects built on the name
senses.titleCN: 以该词构成的各分支学科
senses.definition: fields formed by joining a prefix to the subject, such as the physics of stars, of the earth or of living things
senses.definitionCN: 在学科名称前加前缀构成的领域，如研究星体、地球或生物的那几门
senses.example: Astrophysics applies the methods of physics to stars.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理把物理学的方法用于星体。
senses.why: A method that works on one scale invites use on every scale, so the name becomes a suffix for whole new fields.
senses.whyCN: 在一个尺度上有效的方法会被用到所有尺度，于是这个名字成了新领域的后缀。

senses.title: A course and a textbook
senses.titleCN: 一门课程与一本教科书
senses.definition: the school or university subject as it is taught, examined and written up
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里被教授、考核与编写成书的那门科目
senses.example: She took physics in her first year and chemistry in her second.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一年修物理，第二年修化学。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a subject when it acquires a syllabus, and the same noun then names the room, the hour and the book.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问获得教学大纲后就成了科目，同一个名词于是也命名教室、课时与课本。

senses.title: The mechanism behind an outcome
senses.definition: the practical cause-and-effect chain that makes something happen, used in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的实际因果链条，用于日常口语
senses.example: The physics of the market is not the same as the physics of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的运作机制与桥梁的运作机制并不相同。
senses.why: Speakers borrow the word whenever they want to say that something has a mechanism rather than a mystery.
senses.whyCN: 说话者借用这个词，是想说某事有一套机制，而不是一个谜。

senses.title: Natural philosophy in older use
senses.definition: the older name for the study of nature, before the modern sciences separated
senses.definitionCN: 现代各门科学分化之前，研究自然的学问的旧称
senses.example: Newton wrote his great work under the old name for physics.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿以物理学的旧称写下他的巨著。
senses.why: Before disciplines divided, the study of nature was one subject, and its old title is still visible in the word's ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 在各学科分化之前，对自然的研究是一门学问，它的旧称仍可见于这个词的来历。

intro.en: Physics comes from Greek phusis 'nature', through Latin physica 'natural things'. English first used physic for medicine, and later took physics for natural science, so the two forms parted company.
intro.cn: physics 出自希腊语 phusis「自然」，经由拉丁语 physica「自然之物」传入。英语先用 physic 指医学，后来用 physics 指自然科学，两种形式从此分道。

items.en: Phuein 'to grow, bring forth' is the verb at the root of the family, and it describes what comes into being by itself.
items.cn: phuein 意为「生长、产生」，是这个词族的根动词，描述自行生成之物。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, as opposed to what is made by craft.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，与人以技艺造作之物相对。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises on nature, and the phrase became the name of the subject.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德论自然诸篇的标题，这个说法后来成为学科名称。

items.en: Latin physica, a neuter plural, named natural science, and it passed into English in that form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 是中性复数，指自然科学，并以这一形式进入英语。

items.en: In English physic first meant the art of healing, because medicine studied the natural body; that sense survives in the word for a doctor.
items.cn: 在英语中，physic 起初指医术，因为医学研究的是自然身体；这一意思残留在表示医生的那个词里。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the plural form was used for natural science, while the singular stayed with medicine. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，复数形式用来指自然科学，单数形式则留在医学。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature but has split into medicine, body build and the adjective; the second group places the subject among neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，但已分成医学、体格与形容词；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的科学之中。

entries.definition: The art of healing, now archaic; it is the same source word, but it named medicine rather than the science of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 医术，现已古旧；它是同一个来源词，但命名的是医学，而不是研究物质的科学。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a person's body; it comes from the same Greek root but through French, and names a frame rather than a field.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形态与力量；它出自同一希腊词根，但经法语传入，命名的是体格而不是学科。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body, as opposed to the mental; it describes a kind of thing, while the entry word names a science.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的，与心理的相对；它描述一类事物，而本词命名一门科学。

entries.definition: A person trained in the subject; the suffix marks the practitioner rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 受过该学科训练的人；后缀标示从业者，而不是领域。

entries.definition: Any science of the physical world, including biology, chemistry and geology; the entry word is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界的任何科学，包括生物学、化学与地质学；本词是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of bodies and the forces acting on them; it is a branch of the entry subject rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物体及作用其上的力；它是本学科的一个分支，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: Sciences of non-living systems, such as physics and chemistry; the phrase is broader and excludes biology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究非生命系统的科学，如物理与化学；这个说法更宽，但不包括生物学。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge obtained by observation and experiment; it covers every discipline, of which the entry word is one.
entries.definitionCN: 经观察与实验获得的系统知识；它覆盖所有学科，本词是其中之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the Latin plural for natural things, real derived words and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、拉丁语中表示「自然之物」的复数、真实派生词与真实分支名称。

normal.en: The root means nature, so the subject begins as the study of what happens by itself.
normal.cn: 词根意为「自然」，因此这门学科起初研究自行发生之事。

normal.en: The family runs physical, physically, physicist, astrophysics and metaphysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理的、身体上、物理学家、天体物理与形而上学。

normal.en: The older singular meant medicine, which is why a doctor and a scientist share a root.
normal.cn: 较早的单数形式指医学，所以医生与科学家共有一个词根。

normal.en: The subject splits into classical and modern halves, and into branches named by a prefix.
normal.cn: 这门学科分成经典与现代两半，也分成由前缀命名的各分支。

normal.en: A pendulum and a lens obey the same laws, which is the promise the word makes.
normal.cn: 单摆与透镜服从同一批定律，这正是这个词所许诺的事。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum at the top of its arc, a thermometer beside it and a prism splitting light, all waiting to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摆锤停在弧线的最高点，旁边是温度计，还有一块分光的棱镜，都在等着被测量。

abstract.en: Picture a single law written on a card, held up against two completely different experiments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片上写着一条定律，被举到两组完全不同的实验面前。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose trunk is nature and whose branches are named after stars, rocks and living cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，树干是「自然」，枝干则以星体、岩石与活细胞命名。

examples.en: The physics of the atmosphere explains why the balloon rose so fast.
examples.cn: 大气的物理原理解释了气球为何上升得那么快。

examples.en: He studied physics before turning to the history of science.
examples.cn: 他先修物理，后来转向科学史。

examples.en: No law of physics forbids the machine, only the cost does.
examples.cn: 没有物理定律禁止这台机器，只是成本不允许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹克斯」——「费」力气去「测」：摆锤、棱镜、温度计，量的都是同一件事，这就是物理。

root: 希腊语 phuein「生长、产生」→ phusis「自然」→ ta phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics。较早的英语形式 physic 指医学，后复数形式专指自然科学；这一分开的年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings radiate from one discipline. The subject itself comes first, then the practical physics of a single thing, then its classical core, its modern extensions, its branch subjects, its life as a course, its looser use for any mechanism, and its older name as natural philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一门学科辐射开。先是学科本身，其次是某件具体事物的运作原理，再其次是它的经典内核、现代扩展、各分支学科、作为课程的存在、泛指任何机制的宽松用法，以及它作为「自然之学」的旧名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swinging pendulum beside instruments that all measure the same interaction.
core.cn: 核心意象：摆动的摆锤，旁边是一同测量同一种相互作用的仪器。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the whole discipline, and the same thing as a course and a textbook.
branches.cn: 学科：整体学问，以及它作为课程与教科书的存在。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: how one thing works, and the everyday use of the word for any causal chain.
branches.cn: 机制：某物如何运作，以及日常口语中用这个词泛指任何因果链。

branches.en: CLASSICAL CORE: bodies at ordinary speeds, governed by the older laws.
branches.cn: 经典内核：日常速度下的物体，由较早的定律支配。

branches.en: MODERN EDGE: what happens at extreme speed, mass or smallness.
branches.cn: 现代边缘：在极端速度、质量或微小尺度下发生的事。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND ANCESTOR: prefix-named fields, and the older single study of nature.
branches.cn: 分支与祖先：以前缀命名的各领域，以及较早的那门统一的自然之学。

intro.en: The family comes from a Greek verb for growing, through a Greek noun for nature and a Latin plural for natural things; English then built adjectives, persons and whole branch names on it.
intro.cn: 这个词族出自一个表示「生长」的希腊动词，经由表示「自然」的希腊名词与表示「自然之物」的拉丁复数，英语再在其上构成形容词、人物名词与整批分支名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below are themselves borrowed from Greek; they carried the subject into English and also left the older word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式本身借自希腊语；它们把这门学科带入英语，也留下了表示医学的那个较早的词。

items.meaning: the science of matter and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与运动的科学
items.example: Physics explains why the apple falls.
items.exampleCN: 物理学的解释了苹果为何下落。

items.example: The physical world obeys measurable laws.
items.exampleCN: 物质世界服从可测量的定律。

items.example: The task is physically demanding.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务对体力要求很高。

items.example: The physicist measured the decay rate.
items.exampleCN: 那位物理学家测量了衰变率。

items.meaning: the art of healing, now archaic
items.example: The old physic book lists herbal remedies.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列着草药方。

items.meaning: the physics of stars and space
items.meaningCN: 研究星体与太空的物理
items.example: Astrophysics studies how stars form.
items.exampleCN: 天体物理研究恒星如何形成。

items.example: Geophysics maps the rock beneath the city.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理测绘城市地下的岩层。

items.example: Biophysics models how proteins fold.
items.exampleCN: 生物物理为蛋白质折叠建立模型。

items.meaning: the study of being, placed after the physical treatises
items.meaningCN: 研究存在的学问，原编排在物理诸篇之后
items.example: The question belongs to metaphysics, not to physics.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于形而上学，而不是物理学。

latinEntries.structure: physica, physicorum (n., neuter plural, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）

definition_zh: 物理学家；物理学研究者
definition_en: a person who studies or is trained in physics, either as a researcher or as a teacher
core_image: 一位研究者站在写满公式的黑板前，手里握着粉笔，桌上摆着被拆开的旧钟表与一块磁铁
scene: 研究所的走廊里，一位研究者正把新的测量结果贴到公告板上，同行围过来争论误差来源。A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
sceneCN: 这里指「以物理学为专业的研究者」，对应第 1 个义项：从事物理研究的人；句意为研究者把测量结果贴到公告板，同行围绕误差来源展开争论。画面要点：黑板上的公式、粉笔、拆开的钟表与磁铁。

pos.zh: 物理学家；物理学研究者（可数，复数指一群从业者）

derivatives.zh: 物理学（由希腊语中表示「自然之物」的复数形式经拉丁语传入，指研究物质与运动的学科）
物理的；身体的（学科名词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）

senses.title: A researcher of matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与能量的研究者
senses.definition: a person whose work is to study matter, motion, energy and the forces between them
senses.definitionCN: 以研究物质、运动、能量及其间的作用力为工作的人
senses.example: A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究者把新的测量结果贴到走廊的公告板上，同行围过来争论他所报告的误差来源。
senses.why: The word joins the name of the discipline to a suffix for a practitioner, so it names a person by the field he works in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把学科名称与表从业者的后缀连在一起，因此它用一个人所从事的领域来命名他。

senses.title: The theorist
senses.definition: one who works mainly with mathematical models and predictions rather than with apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 主要用数学模型与预测工作、而不是与仪器打交道的人
senses.example: The theorist predicted a particle years before it was detected.
senses.exampleCN: 这位理论物理学家在粒子被探测到之前多年就预言了它。
senses.why: The discipline divides between those who write the equations and those who test them, and the same title covers both.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科分成写方程的人与检验方程的人，而同一个称谓覆盖两者。

senses.title: The experimentalist
senses.definition: one who designs instruments and measurements to test predictions or discover new effects
senses.definitionCN: 设计仪器与测量、以检验预言或发现新效应的人
senses.example: The experimentalist spent a decade building the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这位实验物理学家花了十年建造探测器。
senses.why: A prediction that no one can measure remains a guess, so the title also belongs to the person who builds the test.
senses.whyCN: 无人能测量的预言仍然只是猜测，因此这个称谓也属于搭建检验的人。

senses.title: A specialist in a branch
senses.definition: a person who works in a named branch such as astrophysics, geophysics or particle physics
senses.definitionCN: 在天体物理、地球物理或粒子物理等具名分支中工作的人
senses.example: The astrophysicist studies how galaxies collide.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家研究星系如何碰撞。
senses.why: The title combines with branch prefixes, so it multiplies into as many names as the subject has branches.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓可以与分支前缀组合，因此它随学科的分支数量一同增殖。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.definition: a person who teaches physics in a school or university rather than working mainly in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学教物理、而非主要在实验室工作的人
senses.example: The physicist who taught the evening class wrote his own demonstrations.
senses.exampleCN: 教晚间课程的那位物理学家自己编写了演示实验。
senses.why: Teaching is part of the profession, and the same title covers the classroom as well as the bench.
senses.whyCN: 教学是这一职业的一部分，因此同一个称谓既覆盖实验室工作台，也覆盖教室。

senses.title: The natural philosopher in older use
senses.definition: a person who studied nature before the modern disciplines separated, often called a philosopher of nature
